author: groundxero
title: ঋণের দুই নিয়ম: শিল্পপতিরা ঋণখেলাপি হলে ব্যাংকের ‘হেয়ারকাট’, গরীবের দুয়ারে রিকভারি এজেন্ট
content:
মজা কী জানেন, কৃষিঋণ মকুবের প্রশ্ন উঠলেই যে যুক্তিগুলো সার বেঁধে আসে সেগুলো আমাদের মুখস্থ — এতে ঋণ-শৃঙ্খলা নষ্ট হয়, চাষি অভ্যাস খারাপ করে ফেলবেন, করদাতার টাকার অপচয় হয়। অথচ কর্পোরেট রাইট-অফের বেলায় সেই একই জিনিস হয়ে যায় ব্যালান্স শিট পরিচ্ছন্ন করার প্রযুক্তিগত পদ্ধতি — কোনও নৈতিক বিপদ নেই, শৃঙ্খলাভঙ্গ নেই, নাম প্রকাশেরও দরকার নেই।


 


টিংকু  খান্না


 


গত ২৫ অগস্ট দিল্লির ন্যাশনাল কোম্পানি ল ট্রাইব্যুনালের তৃতীয় সদস্য নীলেশ শর্মা যে মতামতটি দিলেন, তাতে গোটা দেশের অর্থনৈতিক সাংবাদিকতা সেদিন এক ধাক্কায় থমকে গিয়েছিল। এসেল তথা জ়ি গোষ্ঠীর প্রতিষ্ঠাতা সুভাষ চন্দ্রের ব্যক্তিগত দেউলিয়া মামলায় স্বীকৃত দাবি ২২,০০৬ কোটি ৫৭ লক্ষ টাকা; অনুমোদিত পুনঃপরিশোধ পরিকল্পনায় ঋণদাতাদের জন্য বরাদ্দ ৬ কোটি ২৫ লক্ষ; প্রক্রিয়ার খরচ ধরে সব মিলিয়ে সাড়ে ছ’ কোটি। শতাংশের হিসেবে আদায় ০.০৩, ছাড় ৯৯.৯৭। মামলাটা অবশ্য নতুন নয়, ইন্ডিয়াবুলস হাউজিং ফিনান্স সেই ২০২২ সালেই বিধির ৯৫ ধারায় প্রক্রিয়া শুরু করেছিল, কারণ সুভাষ চন্দ্র এসেল-সংশ্লিষ্ট গোটা কয়েক কোম্পানির ঋণের ব্যক্তিগত গ্যারান্টার ছিলেন। কিন্তু ২৫ অগস্টের পরের দশটা দিনে যা যা ঘটল, সেটাই আসলে এই লেখার বিষয়। কারণ এটা কেবল একজন মিডিয়া-মালিকের আর্থিক পরিণতির গল্প নয় —  এ দেশে ঋণ জিনিসটা কার বেলায় কেমন আচরণ করে, তার প্রায় নিখুঁত একটা পাঠ।


 


এক।


 


ব্যাখ্যা এল চব্বিশ ঘণ্টায়


 


খবর ছড়ানোর একদিনের মধ্যেই “সরকারি সূত্র” মারফত ব্যাখ্যার একটা বেশ গোছানো সেট বাজারে চলে এল। এটা ঋণ মকুব নয়; তিনি নিজে ঋণ নেননি, গ্যারান্টার ছিলেন মাত্র; মূল ঋণ মঞ্জুরির সময়ে দেওয়া ব্যক্তিগত গ্যারান্টির অঙ্ক ২,৫৭৪ কোটি, বাইশ হাজার নয়; কোম্পানির কাছ থেকে আদায় চলতেই থাকবে; আর সবশেষে, এটা নেহাতই একটা ব্যতিক্রমী ঘটনা, দেউলিয়া বিধির সাধারণ চেহারা নয়।


 


সুভাষ চন্দ্র নিজেও চুপ করে থাকেননি —  ২৭ থেকে ২৯ অগস্টের মধ্যে পরপর বিবৃতি আর ভিডিও বার্তায় তিনি জানালেন, এসেল গোষ্ঠী তাদের প্রায় ৪৫ হাজার কোটি টাকার দায়ের মধ্যে ৪৩ হাজার কোটিই শোধ করে দিয়েছে, আপত্তি জানানো ঋণদাতাদের আসল দাবি বাইশ হাজার কোটি নয় বরং প্রায় ৩,৯৯২ কোটি, এবং তাঁর দেওয়া অধিকাংশ গ্যারান্টি সই হয়েছিল ২০১৯-এর ২৪ জানুয়ারির পরে, যখন গোষ্ঠীর ঋণ খেলাপ ইতিমধ্যেই ঘটে গেছে আর ব্যাঙ্কগুলোই কর্মীদের ভবিষ্যতের কথা বলে তাঁর কাছে গ্যারান্টি চেয়েছিল। নিজের ঋণ, খেলাপ আর পরিশোধের একটা স্বাধীন নিরীক্ষার দাবিও তিনি তুলেছেন। বক্তব্যগুলো নথিভুক্ত থাকা দরকার, এবং সেগুলো নিয়ে তর্কও করা দরকার।


 


তার আগে একটা কথা। এ দেশে বেকারত্বের হিসেব নিয়ে, এনসিআরবি-র পরিসংখ্যান নিয়ে, জনগণনার তারিখ নিয়ে সরকারের কাছ থেকে ব্যাখ্যা পেতে মাসের পর মাস, কখনও বছরের পর বছর লেগে যায়। অথচ একজন সংবাদমাধ্যম-মালিকের দেউলিয়া সংক্রান্ত আদেশের গায়ে ব্যাখ্যার প্রলেপ পড়তে লাগল এক দিন। রাষ্ট্র কার সম্মান রক্ষার জন্য কত তৎপর সেটাও একটা তথ্য, আর সেই তথ্যটা কোনও পরিসংখ্যান-দপ্তরের প্রকাশনায় খুঁজে পাবেন না। ব্যাখ্যার পিছু পিছু নেমে পড়লেন অনুগামীর দল — আগে আইন জানুন, না জেনে মন্তব্য করাই এদের স্বভাব, ফেক নিউজ ছড়াবেন না ইত্যাদি ইত্যাদি। এঁদের কাজের ধরনটা লক্ষ করার মতো, কারণ এঁরা মিথ্যা বলছেন না; এঁরা সঠিক তথ্য দিয়ে ভুল ব্যাখ্যা দাঁড় করাচ্ছেন। কোনও একটা শিরোনামের অসতর্ক শব্দ ধরিয়ে দিয়ে গোটা প্রশ্নটাকেই অবৈধ প্রমাণ করার চেষ্টা, ফ্যাক্ট-চেকের ভাষায় সাজানো একটা প্রতিরক্ষা-ব্যূহ। ফল যা হয় তা হল, আলোচনা প্রশ্নের বিষয়বস্তু থেকে সরে গিয়ে প্রশ্নকর্তার যোগ্যতায় গিয়ে ঠেকে। বিতর্কের খুব পুরনো কৌশল, এবং দুর্ভাগ্যজনকভাবে খুবই কার্যকর।


 


তা ব্যাখ্যায় যা ঢাকা পড়ে না, সেগুলো বলি। ব্যক্তিগত গ্যারান্টি নিছক আনুষ্ঠানিকতা নয় — সরকারি হিসেব মেনে নিলেও ২,৫৭৪ কোটির দায়ও তো মিটছে সাড়ে ছ’ কোটিতে। বড় কর্পোরেট ঋণে ব্যাঙ্ক যে ঝুঁকিটা নেয়, তার একটা বড় ভিত্তিই হল প্রোমোটারের ব্যক্তিগত গ্যারান্টি, অর্থাৎ কোম্পানি ডুবলেও ব্যক্তির সম্পত্তি থেকে কিছুটা উদ্ধার হবে এই বিশ্বাস; কর্পোরেট গভর্ন্যান্সের গবেষকরাও মনে করিয়ে দিচ্ছেন যে আন্তর্জাতিক ব্যাঙ্কিং ব্যবস্থায় এটা খুবই চেনা উপকরণ। সেই উপকরণের বাস্তব মূল্য যদি শূন্যের কাছাকাছি দাঁড়ায়, তবে ব্যাপারটা একজনের ক্ষেত্রে ব্যত্যয় নয়, ব্যবস্থার ভিতরের একটা ফাটল। আর আপত্তিটা তুলেছেন কারা, সেটাও মনে রাখা দরকার — বামপন্থীরা নয়, ঋণদাতারা নিজেরাই। এলআইসি হাউজিং ফিনান্স, ক্যানারা ব্যাঙ্ক, ইউনিয়ন ব্যাঙ্ক অফ ইন্ডিয়া (ইউকে) আর এইচডিএফসি ব্যাঙ্ক পরিকল্পনার বিরুদ্ধে ভোট দিয়েছিল, যদিও তাদের ভোটের ভাগ কুড়ি শতাংশেরও কম, আর পরিকল্পনা পাশ হয়ে যায় ৮০.৮১ শতাংশ ভোটে। আপত্তির কারণ সম্পদের অঙ্ক: আদালতের নথিতে ২০১৭ আর ২০১৮ সালের নিট সম্পদের শংসাপত্রে যে হিসেব — প্রচারিত সংখ্যা অনুযায়ী ৪৫,৮৮৮ কোটি আর ৪০,৫৬২ কোটি — তার পাশে ঘোষিত বর্তমান সম্পদ ৩১ কোটি ৭৯ লক্ষ। সুভাষ চন্দ্রের পাল্টা বক্তব্য, ওই পুরনো হিসেব আসলে গোষ্ঠীর কোম্পানিগুলোর বাজারমূল্য ধরে করা, তাঁর ব্যক্তিগত সম্পদের প্রতিফলন নয়। তর্কটা বৈধ, এবং সেই তর্ক মেটাতেই ঋণদাতারা সম্পদের বিশদ ফরেনসিক তদন্ত চেয়েছিলেন। তৃতীয় সদস্য মনে করলেন, নিছক এই ব্যবধানই সম্পদ গোপন করার প্রমাণ নয় এবং পরিকল্পনা …

author: rti_admin
title: The Haldwani Purification Ritual and the Untouchability of Presence: Caste, Purity and the Politics of Belonging
content:
Two days after Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge addressed a public rally at Haldwani’s Ramlila Maidan in Uttarakhand on August 8, a shuddhikaran havan was conducted at the same venue. Members of the Shri Ram Sena Dharmarth Seva Nyas Sangathan performed the ritual to purify the site. The organisation cited the slogans raised at the rally and Kharge’s criticism of the BJP and RSS as its justification for the ceremony. But a political disagreement does not make a public space impure, and it certainly does not justify cleansing a venue after it has been used by a person from the Dalit community. The act reproduced the caste logic of purity and pollution that lies at the heart of untouchability. Kharge subsequently raised the matter in the Rajya Sabha, calling it an experience of untouchability and humiliation and seeking action under the law.

The incident should be called what it is: an expression of caste-based untouchability. The fact that the organisers offered a political justification does not erase the social meaning of the act. A public space was subjected to a ritual of purification after a political event addressed by a person from the Dalit community. In a society where Dalit communities have historically been treated as polluting and subjected to exclusion on that basis, such a ritual reproduces an idea that should have no place in a democratic society. Political disagreement can be answered with argument, protest, or criticism. It cannot justify treating a space as impure because of who has occupied it.

Purification is never simply about cleanliness. It establishes a boundary between what is considered pure and what is considered impure. In the caste order, this distinction has historically been imposed upon human beings themselves. Certain communities were treated as closer to ritual purity, while others were placed at the bottom of the hierarchy and treated as polluting. Their touch, presence and proximity were regulated accordingly. The Haldwani incident brings this logic into a contemporary public space. A person from the Dalit community addressed a political gathering, and the venue was subsequently subjected to a purification ritual. The symbolism is unmistakable: something associated with the event was treated as requiring cleansing. When such a ritual follows the presence of a person from a community historically subjected to notions of pollution, it reproduces the very social imagination that sustains untouchability. This is why the incident deserves criticism not merely as an act of political provocation, but as an act that reproduces caste hierarchy. It is not necessary for the organisers to explicitly announce that Kharge’s caste was the reason for the purification for the caste meaning of the act to matter. Caste often survives through symbols, rituals and practices whose social meaning is inherited from a much longer history. The caste system does not merely divide society into communities. It ranks those communities. The distinction between purity and pollution has historically provided one of the mechanisms through which this ranking is maintained. It determines who can enter certain spaces, who can share food and water, whose touch is acceptable, whose presence is welcome, and whose presence must be kept at a distance.

The most disturbing feature of this system is that impurity is attached to birth. A person is not treated as impure because of an individual action but because of the caste into which they were born. Caste therefore turns social difference into inherited hierarchy and makes inequality appear natural.

Untouchability is the most brutal expression of this logic. It transforms the body into a marker of social status. The question is no longer simply who a person is as an individual, but what caste the person’s body is understood to represent. When a public space is purified after a person from the Dalit community has occupied it, the act invokes this same logic. It suggests that the presence of a particular social body has altered the status of the space. That is the caste imagination that must be confronted.

The distinction between the sacred and the profane provides another way to understand why purification is so significant. Societies create boundaries around what they consider sacred, pure, and worthy of protection. The problem begins when these boundaries are transferred from objects and rituals to human beings. Caste has historically transformed this distinction …

author: Roy Barbosa
title: ‘DOLE, itigil ang drama! Wage increase, ipatupad na!” – KMU
content:
Sa halip na ipatupad ang umiiral na NCR Wage Order No. 27 na inilabas ng Regional Tripartite Wages and Productivity Board-National Capital Region noong Hunyo 23, naglabas ng panibagong Wage Order No. 28 na nagbawas sa dapat sanang dagdag-sahod ng mga manggagawa mula P85 tungong P60.

Ayon sa WO 27, ang P85 na dagdag-sahod ay ilalabas sa magkahiwalay na tranche: P60 simula Hulyo 25 ng kasalukuyang taon at P25 simula Enero 20 sa susunod na taon. Mismong si Department of Labor and Employment Secretary Francis N. Tolentino ang nagsabing tinatayang 1.1 milyong minimum-wage earners ang makakabenepisyo sa naturang dagdag-sahod.

Ngunit sinuspinde naman ang pagpapatupad nito kaugnay sa temporary restraining order (TRO) at kalaunan ay writ of preliminary injunction mula sa Pasig Regional Trial Court bunsod ng mga petisyon mula sa Readycon Trading and Construction Corp. at R-II Builders.

Iginigiit ng Defend Jobs Philippines na mahalagang tingnan ang lawak ng operasyon ng mga kumpanyang kumukuwestiyon sa wage increase, partikular ang Readycon Trading and Construction Corp.

Ang Readycon Trading & Construction Corp. ay isang construction company na nasa industriya mula pa noong 1988. Kabilang sa mga serbisyo nito ang asphalt paving, highway construction, ready-mix asphalt at concrete, construction materials at equipment rental. Mayroon din itong AAAA classification sa ilalim ng Philippine Contractors Accreditation Board (PCAB), ang pinakamataas na contractor category sa bansa.

Kabilang sa mga pribado nitong kliyente ang Ayala Corporation, Bell Construction, C&F Construction, I.M. Construction, Hony Trading & Construction, Red Matrix Builders, Persan Construction at Sta. Clara, bukod sa iba pa. Mayroon din itong mga concrete supply project para sa Meralco Industrial Engineering Services Corporation, Super Globe at Frankhaus International Corporation. Kabilang din sa government clients at projects nito ang mga kontrata para sa Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) at Manila International Airport Authority (MIAA).

Sa mga rekord ng MIAA, nakalistang winning contractor ang Readycon para sa Rapid Exit Taxiways – Civil Works na nagkakahalaga ng P212.802 milyon; Repair and Maintenance of Asphalt Pavement na P50 milyon; Repair and Upgrading of Taxiway Hotel and Charlie na P881.415 milyon; at Repair and Overlay of Runway 06/24 – Civil Works na P540.783 milyon.

Kung pagsasamahin, nasa humigit-kumulang P1.685 bilyon ang listed contract value ng apat na proyekto.

Bukod pa, naging contractor din ang Readycon sa rehabilitation ng J.W. Diokno Boulevard na may contract amount na P185.26 milyon para sa asphalt overlay ng pangunahing kalsada noong 2024. Sa sumunod na taon naman, isang DPWH project sa Antipolo na nagkakahalaga ng P37.98 milyon ang may Readycon bid para sa installation ng safety roller barrier system sa kahabaan ng Sumulong Highway. Idineklara itong lowest calculated responsive bid at inirekomenda para sa award sa kumpanya.

Para sa DJP, hindi sapat na tingnan lamang ang labor cost bilang dagdag na gastos ng employer; anila, dapat ding suriin ang kapasidad ng mga kumpanyang nagbibigay ng serbisyo sa mga proyektong nagkakahalaga ng daan-daang milyon o bilyun-bilyong piso na magbigay ng mas mataas na sahod sa mga manggagawa.

“Kung ang isang kumpanya ay may kakayahang humawak ng mga proyektong nagkakahalaga ng daan-daang milyon at bilyun-bilyong piso…BAKIT ANG ₱60 DAGDAG-SAHOD ANG KAILANGANG ISAKRIPISYO? Hindi natin sinasabing libre ang business operations. Hindi natin sinasabing ang project value ay profit. Ang sinasabi natin: MAY GASTOS ANG PRODUKSYON. At kasama sa produksyon ang paggawa ng manggagawa,” ani DJP.

Kung pagbabatayan ang P60 mula sa unang tranche ng WO No. 27 at ang tinatayang 1.1 milyong minimum-wage earners sa NCR, nasa humigit-kumulang P2.1 bilyon ang halaga ng dagdag-sahod na hindi pa natatanggap ng mga manggagawa batay sa tinatayang 32 araw na dapat sana itong naipatupad.

Sa kabilang banda, giit ng Defend Jobs Philippines maging ng iba’t ibang grupo ng mga manggagawa ang kagyat na pagbibigay ng umento sa sahod na hindi nakabinbin sa sinasabing “tranches”.

“Ang P85 dagdag-sahod sa ilalim ng Wage Order No. 27 ay hindi dapat nakabitin. Hindi ito pabor. Mas lalong hindi ito limos. Ito ay bunga ng pakikibaka ng manggagawa at dapat nang ipatupad!” pahayag ng Defend Jobs Philippines.

Nagbigay rin ng pahayag ang Kilusang Mayo Uno kay DOLE Sec. Tolentino.

“Tolentino, tubuan ka sana ng gulugod at itigil …

author: Rojava IC
title: Sleeper-Cell Report July 2026 – Global Coalition reports 0 confirmed ISIS attacks
content:
An ISIS flag was raised on a school building in al-Zubari, eastern Deir ez-Zor countryside


 


Key Points


– Six sleeper-cell attacks recorded by RIC, but the Global Coalition claims 0 attacks were officially claimed by ISIS


– One military personnel was killed, and a further five injured


– A minimum of seven alleged ISIS members were arrested


– A total of 36 civilians were injured, two killed


– An ISIS flag was raised on a school building in Deir ez-Zor


–

Two Tunisian families linked to ISIS mercenaries repatriated from Roj camp


 


In-Depth


In July of 2026, RIC

recorded six sleeper-cell attacks which some publications have attributed to ISIS, according to


North Press Agency

 one of these attacks was claimed by ISIS whereas the


Global Coalition


reported that July was the first month since the territorial defeat of ISIS in 2019, where they claimed 0 attacks. Also this month at least 7 members of ISIS cells were arrested.


On July 7, Bombings struck central Damascus near the Ministry of Tourism and the Four Seasons Hotel, during the visit of Macron the president of France to Syria. Ministry of Interior has attributed the attack to ISIS, the bombing resulted in the killing of one civilian and injury of 36.


On July 8, three attacks happened during the same day and the are believed to have been carried out by ISIS members.

Unidentified gunmen on a motorcycle used machine guns to target an oil truck in Abrahyah town in eastern Deir ez-Zor countryside, killing the driver.


Similarly, unidentified gunmen on a motorcycle, attacked a checkpoint of the Internal Security Forces near al-Baserah city bridge.


According to North Press Agency, also on July 8 ISIS

claimed responsibility for the killing of Rashad Khalaf al-Ghurair in the northern countryside of Deir ez-Zor.


On July 15,

unknown gunmen on a motorcycle opened fire on a member of the 72nd Division on the road linking al-Arimah and Manbij in eastern Aleppo countryside, injuring the him.


On July 18,

two unidentified gunmen on a motorcycle opened fire directly on member of the Defence Ministry


near al-Awsajli junction in eastern Manbij city.


On July 9,

Syria’s Interior Ministry announced its security forces had dismantled several ISIS cells in southern Syria, arresting a senior leader and several members accused of involvement in assassinations and financing terror.


On July 28,

Syrian Internal Security Forces and the General Intelligence Service in Aleppo announced the arrest of individuals allegedly affiliated with the ISIS, during a security operation in Aleppo and its surrounding countryside.


An ISIS flag was raised on a school building in al-Zubari, eastern Deir ez-Zor countryside, in an incident that sparked widespread concern among residents.


During July, Two Tunisian families linked to ISIS were repatriated from


Roj Camp, which houses families of ISIS members, and returned to Tunisia. Additionally, Tunisian citizen Bilal Chawachi was sentenced to 55 years in prison after being convicted on terrorism-related charges, specifically traveling to Syria and fighting alongside the extremist organization.


Germany sentenced an Iraqi man to life imprisonment and his former wife to nine years and six months in prison after convicting them of enslaving and torturing two Yazidi girls while they were members of ISIS in Syria and Iraq between 2015 and 2017.


Three U.S. citizens pleaded guilty to terror charges, prosecutors said the defendants communicated through encrypted messaging applications between July and November 2025 and planned to travel to Turkey before crossing into Syria to join ISIS. 


* Due to the low rate of confirmed ISIS attacks RIC has decided to stop publishing monthly sleeper-cell reports and instead share a bi-annual summary of ISIS activity throughout Syria.

author: Unknown
title: Iranian female trainer sentenced to prison
content:
Nergis Haydari, a fitness and bodybuilding trainer in the city of Izeh who was detained by the Intelligence Organization of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps during protests in Iran in January, was sentenced to five years in prison by the Revolutionary Court in Ahvaz on charges of “engaging in activities against national security.”


Nergis Haydari was also sanctioned for failing to comply with mandatory hijab rules during sports activities and for sharing these activities with the public.

author: Bulatlat Contributors
title: Groups in Eastern Visayas welcome arrest of Romualdez
content:
“While the Romualdezes are reveling in their stolen wealth, the people of Eastern Visayas struggle with extreme food insecurity.”

TACLOBAN CITY – Progressive groups from Eastern Visayas welcomed the arrest of Leyte First District Representative and former House Speaker Ferdinand Martin Romualdez over charges of plunder.

In a statement, Bagong Alyansang Makayan (Bayan) Sinirangan Bisayas considered Romualdez’s arrest as a win for the Filipino people. “It’s been a year since we have incessantly marched the streets to protest the widespread corruption and finally, key players of ghost flood control projects like Romualdez are now being held accountable.”

While the group welcomed the warrants of arrest issued to Martin Romualdez and former Ako Bicol Representative Zaldy Co, they said that the magnitude of such corruption extends beyond Co and Romualdez and could have not been carried out by only two or four individuals. “The testimonies and revelations of Co and DPWH Undersecretary Roberto Bernardo points to a much wider network of officials involved. Most seriously, Ferdinand Marcos Jr. tolerated and benefited from the scheme,” Bayan Alyansang Makabayan said in a statement. Bayan also challenged both Co and Romualdez to reveal the full extent of the conspiracy and all individuals involved. “The government must follow the money, identify every official and private individual who participated in or benefited from the scheme, and ensure they are punished.”

“The Romualdez clan is a political dynasty closely tied to the Marcoses. Martin’s father, Benjamin “Kokoy” Romuadez, the younger brother of Imelda Marcos, served as Leyte Governor, and later appointed as ambassador to the United States, China, and Saudi Arabia during the Marcos dictatorship, was in cahoots with the Marcoses in embezzling public funds,” Bayan-SB said. As First District Representative of Leyte, Martin Romualdez received a total of P57 billion of funds from the Department of Public Works and Highways from 2023 until 2026, the highest among all legislative districts in the country. Despite this, Bayan-SB noted that “the people of Leyte and Eastern Visayas still suffer from skyrocketing prices and measly wages”. “While the Romualdezes are reveling in their stolen wealth, the people of Eastern Visayas struggle with extreme food insecurity,” said Bayan-SB.

Kabataan Partylist Tacloban Chapter Chairperson Rejomar Baltar, in an interview with Bulatlat, said that Filipinos should stay vigilant and continuously call for the arrest of all the politicians involved in large-scale corruption. “We have to remain cautious of Marcos Jr.’s attempt to escape accountability. Corrupt officials must be held accountable from Romualdez, Co, and even Marcos Jr,” he said.

“The youth of Tacloban and Eastern Visayas will not stop until all the masterminds and enablers of the anomalous flood control projects are put behind bars,” said Baltar. (AMU, RVO)

author: Brian Hioe
title: When Will the American Commentariat Give Up on Asking When Taiwan Will Give Up?
content:
“WILL TAIWAN JUST GIVE UP?” by Simon Shuster in The Atlantic is the latest article in the heady genre of articles by white men who visit Taiwan for a few days, speak only to elite political actors, and decide that they have arrived at the final verdict on Taiwan’s fate. All the more hilarious that the article contains several glaring factual errors, has large gaps in logic as well as evident bias, and renders judgments based on vibes-based thinking more than anything else.

Fittingly, Shuster opens with two paragraphs of fawning awe over Chinese President Xi Jinping. From this, one generally has a sense that Shuster is simply taken in by the pomp and circumstance that China has sought to project with its state institutions. No surprise, then, that when Taiwan’s legislature appears in the piece, some three-quarters through the piece, as compared to the grandeur of a dictator, it is described only as a “drab building on a narrow street in the center of Taipei.”

Shuster then goes on to describe how he is unimpressed with the comparative lack of security in the legislature. One wonders how Shuster would have felt had he been subjected to an invasive and humiliating security search, such as he perhaps would have faced in China. But Shuster is positively fascinated by China’s authoritarian grandeur and the “winking, elliptical ways” of the “Chinese Communist Party, like its forebear in the Soviet Union”. Taiwan, of course, as a contemporary democracy, is simply boring by comparison.

It is from there that Shuster moves toward his assessment of Taiwan’s military defense. Shuster first is overly impressed by an AI-generated video released by the People’s Liberation Army (PLA)–which includes marching humanoid robots–as though this were any indication of military reality. Then, Shuster goes on to describe the war outlook in the following terms:

“Taiwan has more than 200,000 active military personnel, and they could probably fend off a Chinese attack for a short while. But within a few weeks, the U.S., Japan, and other allies would need to resupply the island with fuel and weapons. The Chinese navy—the world’s largest fleet of warships—would do its best to keep them away. Cargo traffic through the Taiwan Strait, one of the world’s main shipping channels, would be interrupted, wiping trillions of dollars in value from global markets. If the U.S. goes to war with China to defend Taiwan, the likely death toll of soldiers and civilians would be in the tens of thousands on both sides. War games have consistently shown that, in a conventional conflict, the U.S. military could expect to lose more troops in the initial weeks of fighting than it lost over the course of 20 years in Iraq and Afghanistan.”

Shuster raises various anecdotes about meetings with Taiwanese government officials, defense industry executives, and current or former members of the military in which they raise frank assessments of the limitations that Taiwan’s military currently has. It is hard not to see why they might make such comments to Shuster, perhaps hoping that his article would shake up Taiwan’s military to further preparedness, and encourage the US to stronger support of Taiwan. Not long prior to the publication of Shuster’s piece, the KMT appeared to reverse course in short order on funding for drones after becoming intimidated by an article in The Economist, perhaps such sources were hoping for the same.

For all his preoccupation with Chinese optics, the Chinese military is then curiously absent from the rest of Shuster’s article after this point. It never seems to occur to Shuster that perhaps the Chinese military is not as strong as it seeks to project, with China having not fought a war in 47 years. Simply by virtue of geography, an invasion of Taiwan that involves a beachhead landing would involve tens of thousands of casualties and have a catastrophic economic impact on the region–regardless of whether the US intervenes or not.

A naval blockade or quarantine, then, may be more likely, but would still be an act of war. China’s own shipping lanes, as well as those of other powers in the region, such as Japan and the Philippines, would be impacted. In this sense, a blockade would also pose a risky move for China if Taiwan is able to weather a blockade beyond what is tenable for China. It would also be improbable that other powers in the region would simply sit still when a blockade impacts their own economies and destabilizes the region; one …

author: Dominic Gutoman
title: Public memory of ‘drug war’ killings survives
content:
A decade of human rights violations is documented in an exhibit launched by Dekada, a coalition of victims’ families, human rights organizations, and allies, running from August 14 to September 5, 2026.

The exhibit serves as a living archive and memorial to the victims and their bereaved families, with artists, journalists, and advocacy groups helping build a space for solidarity and collective remembrance.

It has been ten years since Oplan Tokhang was implemented under the administration of Rodrigo Duterte, yet justice remains elusive for families of victims in the Philippines.

Duterte is currently in the custody of the International Criminal Court after it found reasonable grounds to believe that he bears responsibility for widespread killings during his terms as Davao City mayor and president. His trial is set to begin on November 30, 2026. (Video report by Dominic Gutoman/Bulatlat)

author: Editors
title: 9/11: How the US turned tragedy into barbarity
content:
Twenty-five years ago, the world changed irrevocably. Not because terrorists from the al-Qaeda network attacked the United States, bringing down the World Trade Center’s Twin Towers in New York, hitting the Pentagon in Virginia and killing nearly 3,000 people. It changed because of US imperialism’s response.

The day after 9/11, the editors of

Socialist Alternative

 magazine, one of the precursor publications of

Red Flag

, warned: “The real threat to people around the world is not terrorism, but the racism, militarism, repression and nationalism that has been unleashed in the wake of the terrorist attacks”.

A week later, President George W. Bush, in an address to a joint session of Congress, announced his so-called War on Terror: “Every nation, in every region, now has a decision to make. Either you are with us, or you are with the terrorists”. His administration rode the wave of outrage over al-Qaeda’s assault to open a new era of imperialist aggression that has cost millions of people’s lives. 

First came Afghanistan in October. It didn’t matter that the ruling Taliban

offered to hand over Osama bin Laden

, the alleged mastermind of the terrorist attacks, to a neutral country to face trial. The US was interested only in war. Condoleezza Rice, then Bush’s national security adviser, admitted as much to the

New Yorker

’s Nicholas Lemann several months later. In the wake of the 9/11 attacks, she had asked senior national security staff to think about how to “capitalise on these opportunities”. 

The Bush administration soon began making a public case for invading Iraq—which had no ties to 9/11—declaring the country part of an “axis of evil” with Iran and North Korea. Undersecretary of State John Bolton soon expanded the axis list to include Cuba, Libya and Syria. The bombs started raining down on Baghdad in March 2003.

These invasions would have been followed by more had the resistance in Iraq not bogged down the US military in an intractable counterinsurgency. Nevertheless, Brown University’s

Costs of War research

 estimates the direct death toll from US military operations in the post-9-11 era in Iraq, Afghanistan, Syria, Yemen and Pakistan to be close to 1 million people. It estimates a further 3.6 to 3.8 million “indirect” deaths resulting from the “destruction of economies, healthcare systems, infrastructure and the environment”. 

The US also set up a global kidnapping network, which it termed “extraordinary rendition”, and a series of “black sites” in which prisoners were held without charge and tortured.

The Open Society Foundation estimates

 that 54 governments collaborated in the program. Then there is the notorious

Guantánamo Bay torture camp

, used since 2002 and still holding ageing prisoners from the War on Terror. This all served as notice that the US empire would stop at nothing to maintain its global domination.

A more enduring legacy of this era of “forever wars” has been the construction of vast internal security and surveillance states, which have trampled civil and democratic rights. 

More than 140 governments have adopted “counterterrorism” legislation since 9/11, beginning with the USA PATRIOT Act, which green-lit mass surveillance and delayed-notice search warrants and bolstered spy agency resources. Mega-departments, such as Homeland Security in the US and Home Affairs in Australia, were established as Western states have become more authoritarian.

Indeed, Australia is one of the worst offenders. “No other nation can match the volume of Australia’s counter-terrorism laws”, wrote legal academics Rebecca Ananian-Welsh and Keiran Hardy in

a 2021 piece for the University of Queensland’s

Contact

 magazine

. They describe the scope of the laws as “staggering”, “unprecedented” and “extreme”, noting that they go beyond even “historical wartime powers”.

They include control orders, preventive detention, and compulsory retention of all telecommunication and online data of every resident. The

Surveillance Legislation Amendment (Identify and Disrupt) Act

 of 2021 gave law enforcement agencies the power to take control of a person’s individual online accounts, modify or delete their data and even take over entire networks. That is, they can legally alter a person’s text messages.

Death and destruction abroad and authoritarianism at home: such is the “rules-based order”, the purported demise of which we are supposed to lament. This post-9/11 era normalised authoritarianism …

author: Susan Price
title: Singapore’s unfinished anti-colonial struggle
content:
The dominant history of modern Singapore was meticulously constructed under the banner of the “Singapore Story”. By presenting the material interests of the ruling elite as the universal interests of the nation, the state narrative reduces the mass anti-imperialist movement of the mid-20th century into a fable; one wherein a heroic bourgeois leadership single-handedly navigates a vulnerable island state through the perils of communism to construct a prosperous capitalist metropolis.

In his six-part oral history series with Pintjin (PJ) Thum, Dr Poh Soo Kai, former student activist, co-founder of the People’s Action Party (PAP) and the Barisan Sosialis (Socialist Front) — and former political prisoner detained for nearly 17 years without trial — delivers a vital historical materialist counter-narrative.

In 36 minutes of personal testimony, Poh unpacks the class dynamics, state coercion, and geopolitical shake-ups that dismantled working-class power and shaped Singapore's transition into a disciplined capitalist state.

Poh begins by recalling how post-World War II Malayan households were adorned with portraits of Indonesia’s Sukarno, India’s Nehru and Gandhi, and China’s Chiang Kai-Shek, who were seen as regional anti-colonial leaders. The struggle in Singapore was bound to broader anti-imperialist movements across Malaya, Indonesia, and Vietnam.

Poh’s account of the 1954 Fajar Trial undermines the state’s origin myth, which positions the trial of eight members of the editorial board of Fajar (Dawn) — the University of Malaya Socialist Club’s newspaper — as Lee Kuan Yew’s (LKY’s) personal legal breakthrough.

[Editor’s note: Harry Lee Kwan Yew co-founded the PAP, was a barrister and opposition figure and became Singapore’s first Prime Minister in 1959.]

As president of the University of Malaya Socialist Club, Poh helped publish Fajar, an anti-colonial paper opposing the anti-communist South East Asian Treaty Organisation (SEATO) and foreign military bases. When the editorial board was charged with sedition, Queen’s Counsel DN Pritt arrived to lead the defense. Poh recounts Pritt greeting him warmly at the Dolphin Hotel before turning to LKY, who was acting as local junior counsel, and saying, “Harry, now you can go.”

Pritt dismissed LKY specifically to formulate an anti-colonial strategy directly with the student activists, recognising that the trial was a political battlefield rather than a legal technicality.

This moment symbolises the clash between the radical student movement and LKY’s legalism, and how official history later repackaged a left-wing victory as an LKY solo masterstroke.

As the PAP rose to power, internal contradictions between its left-wing mass base and moderate leadership erupted.

Poh recounts how the left wing consistently pushed for true self-determination, confronting PAP Chair Toh Chin Chye to issue a public statement supporting then-Chief Minister David Marshall’s 1956 call for internal self-rule — a move that infuriated LKY upon his return from London.

[Editor’s note: Marshall was appointed Chief Minister after contesting the 1955 election as a candidate for the Labour Front. After failing to secure self-rule, he resigned as Chief Minister in June 1956.]

Chief Minister Lim Yew Hock’s violent crackdowns on trade unions and Chinese school students from 1956 onward served a dual purpose: suppressing working-class organisation while allowing LKY to position himself as the sensible alternative acceptable to British imperial interests and local capital.

When dissident MPs and activists walked out to form the Barisan Sosialis in 1961, every PAP branch including LKY’s own Tanjong Pagar constituency defected to the new party. The PAP was left as a hollow electoral vessel without organic mass support.

To preempt an electoral defeat, the state deployed Operation Coldstore in February 1963. Officially framed as a security operation against a communist plot tied to the 1962 Brunei Revolt, Coldstore was a draconian political purge that sought to decapitate the political opposition, dismantle union leadership and ensure PAP hegemony.

The state weaponised identity politics to divide the multi-ethnic working-class by branding Chinese-educated labour leaders and Barisan Sosialis members as “Chinese chauvinists”. It replaced class-based solidarity with state-directed multiracialism that contained labour organising within non-threatening boundaries.

author: AWSM
title: The anarchist case for abstentionism in elections
content:
The right to vote is seen by most as a necessary prerequisite for freedom across the world. People have fought and died for the right to vote in elections. Women across the world fought bitter battles for the right to vote. So why should anarchists question this as a right worth having?

The entire electoral show is designed to encourage us to believe that not only does our vote matter, but that it is the most important decision we could possibly make. Indeed, voting is held so sacred by many that the mere mention of not voting is enough to cause outrage. Pointing out that our vote makes no difference anyway, will see you accused of being apathetic, privileged, immature, and even being part of the alt-right!

But as noted anarchist Vernon Richards wrote,

“So long as we have capitalism and government, the job of anarchists is to fight both, and at the same time encourage people to take what steps they can to run their own lives.” [“Anarchists and Voting,” pp. 176–87, The Raven, No. 14, p. 179].

Electoralism ensures that a statist perspective becomes dominant. Everything is seen in terms of state intervention and following the decisions of the leaders, which has always proved deadly to encouraging a spirit of revolt, self-management, and self-help – the very keys to creating change in a society. Rather than being something other people discuss on behalf of working-class people, anarchists argue that politics should not be a specialised activity in the hands of the so-called experts (i.e., politicians) but instead lie in the hands of those directly affected by it in the process of participation, direct action, and self-management. Those that channel any “political” conclusions into electoral politics distort discussions into only what is possible within the current system. Given this, is it surprising that anarchists argue that the people “must organise their powers apart from and against the State?” [Bakunin, The Political Philosophy of Bakunin, p. 376].

Abstentionists get told, “If you don’t vote, you have no right to complain about the outcome,” but we consider the opposite to be true. It is those who have voted, who have agreed to the rules, and agreed to be governed by the winners who cannot complain. It is those who do not participate who have the right to complain about the outcome more than anyone else.

We get told that the reality is that voting does change things, but we can, and do, deny that. Voting attempts to provide the population with the illusion of change while in reality it reinforces the current system. A policy here and there may change, the faces may change, but the system of a wealthy minority ruling a poorer majority remains. People will continually be telling us that abstaining from voting will help the right-wing win the election, that it is better if the lesser evil wins. This may possibly be the case (although the argument is far from convincing), but why should we base our society on a compromise with evil? In fact, the “progressive” left wing party you vote for will often be ready to take the same actions as a right-wing government when it comes to imposing anti-working-class action upon us, (as we shall show later in this essay the state has a corrupting effect on those who enter politics with high principles). There should be a better way, and we say the dismantling of government, in all its existing and potential forms is that way.

Most of the left wing in Aotearoa, and quite a few people who claim to identify as anarchists, will support reformist parties in the upcoming election. You will hear them saying things like “vote Labour (or Green) without illusions,” or “vote Labour/Green but build a socialist alternative.” The slogans that these others may shout only reflect the idea that change can and should be brought about by a small number of elite politicians. Abstentionists do not say things like this. There are many problems with our electoral system of democracy, which we shall run through, but we must state that first and foremost, as anarchists, we see voting as against running contrary to our anti-statist and anti-hierarchy principles, and we see electoralism as contrary to our goals and practice. It reinforces the idea that society is divided into order-givers and order-takers. Famed French anarchist, Elisee Reclus, put it well when he said,

“Everything that can be said about the suffrage may be summed up in a sentence. To vote is to give up your own power. To elect a …

author: Editors
title: FROM THE ARCHIVE—Tragedy in America: how should the left respond? (12 September 2001)
content:
Today, there is no shortage of mainstream commentators prepared to speak out strongly against the war policy of the George W. Bush era. Even current US President Donald Trump claims to have been an opponent of the Iraq invasion and of the broader orientation of the Republican administration of 2001-09.

But in the days after 9/11, no major media outlet would hear a word against the US. Those of us who said that US imperialism, not terrorism, posed the greatest threat to the world were vilified, marginalised and condemned as terrorist sympathisers.

Socialist Alternative is proud that we took an unequivocal anti-imperialist stance, even in those early and dark days when doing so was deeply unpopular. The article republished below was put out on 12 September 2001. We think its arguments, unlike so much written then and since, stand the test of time.

Socialist Alternative

 magazine editorial

The September 11 attacks in New York and Washington, D.C., are a horrific tragedy.

The bodies of thousands of ordinary working-class people—of all races, religions and political beliefs—lie in the rubble of New York’s World Trade Centre.

But the response of the world’s leaders, and of the media commentators and opinion writers, has been marked by a hideous hypocrisy.

US President George Bush, along with others such as Tony Blair, and our own John Howard and Kim Beazley, have fallen over themselves to condemn terrorism, violence and murder.

They have vowed to fight the “uncivilised” actions of people who they accuse of having no regard for the sanctity of human life. But it is the likes of Bush, Blair and Howard who preside over a system that condemns millions to death and misery all around the world.

Up to 200,000 civilians were murdered in the oil-driven Gulf War in 1991. More than 500,000 children have died since as a result of crippling sanctions.

Around the world—in Indonesia, the Middle East, Africa and Latin America—despotic regimes financed and supported by the US government have slaughtered hundreds of thousands of people.

The genocide of one-third of the East Timorese population was directly supported by the US, Australia and Britain. The brutal Israeli occupation of Palestine is propped up by the $1.5 billion in aid it receives from the US every year.

And the logic of the capitalist system has condemned millions to death through war and poverty around the globe. 20,000 children starve to death and die of preventable diseases every day because US grain is dumped in the ocean to keep prices up, and because multinationals conspire to stop medical treatments being accessible to the world’s poor.

And while George Bush rails against terrorism, the fact is that Bin Laden, accused of being behind the September 11 attacks, shares with Timothy McVeigh the distinction of having been trained in terrorism by the US government.

The CIA trained Bin Laden as a commander in its proxy army that fought the USSR after its invasion of Afghanistan in 1979. Bin Laden was “so effective a recruiter [for the Afghan guerrillas] that close comrades at the time actually thought he was working for the CIA”.

The same US government that today denounces Bin Laden and the Taliban lauded them as “freedom fighters” in the 1980s.

The rulers of the world have no interest in human rights, or in the lives of ordinary people. As Leon Trotsky said over 80 years ago:

“[We have] nothing in common with those bought and paid for moralists who, in response to any terrorist act, make solemn declarations about the ‘absolute value’ of human life. These are the same people who, on other occasions, in the name of other absolute values—for example, the nation’s honour or the monarch’s prestige—are ready to shove millions of people into the hell of war.”

That millions of people around the world passionately hate imperialist US policies is the fault of the US ruling class; of the politicians and businessmen who grow fat through the suffering and death of ordinary people.

The tragedy of the attacks on the US is that ordinary Americans have had to suffer for the genocidal and inhumane policies of their rulers. In answer to the question of where responsibility lies for this senseless loss of life, there can only be one answer: Capitalism.

But whilst we understand the anger directed against America, Marxists are not terrorists.

We utterly oppose the idea that, by killing ordinary people, a tiny minority can change the world for the better. It is only through …

title: “There’s this sketchy Dutch black metal band touring Australia …”
content:
I was contacted a little while ago by somebody raising concerns about a couple of upcoming black metal gigs. Below is the text they sent.

There’s this sketchy Dutch black metal band, Helleruin, playing in Melbourne at the Northcote Social Club on September 11 and in Sydney at Crowbar on September 12.

Most of Helleruin’s records have been released on New Era Productions, which has put out a number of releases by fash black metal bands and which is run by Jasper Velzel, a NSBM and RAC musician. In addition, another project of Helleruin’s Carchost — Orewoet — is on the label Heidens Hart, which — along with releasing some far-right stuff — is owned by a former live guitarist of prominent fash band Graveland.

Moreover, a number of the local supporting acts have sketchy connections.

Order of Orias, one of two supports in Melbourne along with Petrol (see below), are on World Terror Committee, which releases fashy stuff and is owned by Sven Zimper, a member of prominent NSBM group Absurd.

Of the bands playing Sydney with Helleruin (Krvna, Pestilential Shadows, Destruktor, Vicissitude, Gravgöt, Grotesque Bliss, Petrol, Blasfemancia and Akhoth) at the ‘Call from the Grave’ festival:

Pestilential Shadows have released music on the Chinese label, GoatowaRex, who are very friendly to NSBM acts. Additionally, PS is part of a collective called Ordo Ater Anguis/Order of the Black Serpent, which includes numerous far right acts. Michael W Ford of Black Funeral appears to be a former Order of Nine Angles (09A) member in the United States who — after distancing himself from O9A — attempted to formulate a social Darwinist version of the Satanic Temple (lol), which coalesce around the Australian fash-friendly label, Dark Adversary. Indeed, one of the members of PS is also a member of Varw, a band on Dark Adversary. Further, Akhoth released a demo, ‘Storm of Pagan Fury’, on CD on Dark Adversary this year.

Grotesque Bliss are on Iron Bonehead which, along with the suspect name, appears to be run by a (if only barely) crypto-fascist.

Destruktor is on a label, Hells Headbangers, which has previously released and re-released stuff by Satanic Warmaster and Deströyer 666, including re-releasing Deströyer 666’s debut album, ‘Unchain the Wolves’, on a few different mediums over the last few years. Additionally, Inquisition had a few releases on Hells Headbangers after their lead singer (who is also a Satanist pedo) released openly fash music on fash label Satanic Skinhead Propaganda (a label which the Iron Bonehead guy sold in his old fash-friendly record store).

The most recent (2024) EP of Krvna, formally of PS, was released on Zazen Sounds, run by Greek nazi black metaller Acherontass of Αχέροντας (Krvna played guest guitar on their most recent album). For what it’s also worth, Third Eye Temple — the Polish label on which Krvna’s 2022 album was released — have released one split and re-issued an EP by Voidhanger, a side project of Polish far right black metallers, Infernal War.

Finally, Petrol were previously on a cancelled bill with Gurn. The other headliner was Portal, who have released lots of records on Hells Headbangers including, recently, a split with Blood of Kingu — a side-project of the Ukrainian ultra-nationalists from Drudkh — on the label in 2014.
