author: Mattilda Bernstein Sycamore
title: ACT UP in Louisiana Was Pragmatic, Bold, Creative. Let’s Learn From It.
content:
David W. Hylan’s new book Small Town Rage shines a light on ‘90s-era AIDS organizing in conservative Shreveport.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

Nearly four decades have passed since ACT UP (the AIDS Coalition to Unleash Power) started in New York in 1987 as a direct action activist group “united in anger and committed to direct action to end the AIDS crisis.”

The 1980s were a time of mass death and government inaction, and ACT UP responded with confrontational protests that disrupted business as usual to force change. ACT UP’s tactics have become legendary, but its swift growth into a movement with over 100 autonomous chapters in cities large and small across the U.S., as well as in Canada, Europe, and Australia, has largely disappeared from the public record. There are however several chapters that continue today, including in New York, Philadelphia, Paris, and London, and new chapters that have emerged in Pittsburgh, Cleveland, and Chicago to respond to draconian cuts in HIV/AIDS services and trans health care under the second Trump administration.

In Small Town Rage: Fighting Back in the Deep South, David W. Hylan shines the light on ACT UP Shreveport, which started in 1990 in a conservative Louisiana town far from the centers of institutional power. Based on dozens of interviews with ACT UP Shreveport participants that he conducted for his 2016 movie of the same name (co-directed with Raydra Hall), the book expands the narrative to show how activists in Shreveport organized in a hostile environment to transform the situation for people with HIV/AIDS.

In our current regressive political climate, which eerily echoes the conservative backlash of the 1980s and ‘90s (don’t forget that it was Ronald Reagan who first used the campaign slogan “Make America Great Again”), ACT UP Shreveport’s legacy of resistance in the Bible Belt couldn’t be more relevant. In the interview that follows, Hylan discusses covert and overt organizing strategies, conflicts within the group, coalition actions, and confronting AIDS organizations, religious bigotry, and the KKK.

Mattilda Bernstein Sycamore: When people first started publicizing ACT UP Shreveport meetings, it was done through existing relationships. Deborah Allen, one early member, made cards with the meeting time that people could hand discreetly across the table as an invitation to join. I’m struck both by the need for caution, and the intimacy in this encounter, and I wonder if you could speak to other innovations ACT UP Shreveport made to deal with the intense homophobia of Shreveport at the time.

David W. Hylan: The cards Deborah made really capture what organizing in Shreveport required at the time. You have to remember that visibility carried consequences. People could lose jobs, relationships with their families, their churches, even their housing. So they couldn’t necessarily organize the way ACT UP could in New York, where you could put up a poster announcing a meeting and expect people to show up.

A lot of ACT UP Shreveport’s early organizing depended on trust. One person knew another person who might be angry enough, frightened enough, or simply fed up enough to get involved. Those cards could be passed quietly from one person to another without forcing someone to publicly identify themselves. But what is interesting is that this caution existed alongside some very public activism.

Once ACT UP Shreveport decided to act, its members could be extraordinarily visible. They papered The Shreveport Times, protested public officials, challenged the medical establishment, confronted the Klan, blocked the Red River bridge, and used sidewalk chalk and flyers to put AIDS and gay people into spaces where Shreveport would have preferred not to see them.

So there was almost a dual strategy: protect people when they needed protection, but refuse to allow that fear to make the movement invisible. They learned how to operate within the culture they were confronting rather than simply importing an ACT UP model from somewhere else.

You write that in Shreveport, “Church wasn’t optional, it was cultural law.” And, “Religion was not just belief; it was enforcement.” So the judgment and condemnation from the pulpit was embedded in every interaction. How did ACT UP challenge this?

Religion in Shreveport was complicated because ACT UP wasn’t simply challenging …

author: Shireen Akram-Boshar
title: CUNY Discloses Investments in Israeli Apartheid After Years-Long Campaign
content:
CUNY has direct investments in weapons manufacturers enabling Israel’s genocide, including Boeing and Lockheed Martin.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

On Wednesday, September 9, activists from CUNY4Palestine broadcast their findings regarding the City University of New York’s (CUNY) investment portfolio in a press conference in front of New York City Hall.

“Following years of campus organizing and after a wave of demonstrations that erupted to protest CUNY’s complicity in the ongoing genocide in Gaza, the students have won disclosure!” the student group said in a statement shared with Truthout.

CUNY has now disclosed its ties to companies profiting from Israel’s crimes – including Boeing, Lockheed Martin, and Northrop Grumman.

The fight for disclosure is just a stepping stone in the larger struggle across the U.S. to compel academic institutions to divest from companies complicit in Israel’s crimes.

In mid-August, CUNY agreed to settle and disclose its stock and bond holdings by September 2, following a two-year battle with activists. The legal battle began with CUNY4Palestine and CUNY Law Students for Justice in Palestine filing a Freedom of Information Law (FOIL) request in 2024, which was quickly denied by the university. The activist groups then filed a lawsuit demanding that CUNY disclose its investments in companies involved in Israeli apartheid and genocide dating back to January 2020. A judge ruled in 2025 that CUNY could not withhold its records, but the university appealed the ruling. Finally, in August 2026, the university agreed to a settlement that included disclosure.

Corinna Mullin, who was among four adjunct professors fired by CUNY for speaking in solidarity with Palestine in June 2025, spoke at the Wednesday press conference. (Three of those professors have since been reinstated, including Mullin.)

“Let’s be clear – CUNY did not volunteer this information,” Mullin said. “They fought us every step of the way.”

“It took a FOIL lawsuit in the New York Supreme Court, an encampment, speakouts, protests, petitions, demonstrations at board of trustee hearings, and a relentless campaign of pressure” to get the university to disclose, she went on.

“And this campaign, although accelerated by the urgency of the genocide against the Palestinian people started in October 2023, dates back years,” she added.

CUNY4Palestine “has identified numerous investments in CUNY’s portfolio,” the organization explained in the statement, “that confirm CUNY’s direct complicity in colonization, genocide, war crimes, prison labor, border militarization, imperialist military interventions, mass incarceration and fascist attacks on our immigrant communities.”

The university has direct investments in multiple weapons manufacturers involved in Israel’s genocide in Gaza, the activists announced, including over $212,407.10 in unsecured Boeing stocks, $107,488.89 in Boeing common stocks, $141,201.34 in Raytheon stocks, and $65,302.74 in Lockheed Martin stocks.

“Boeing in particular facilitates ongoing massacres in Iran, Lebanon, and Palestine through its manufacturing of F-15 fighter jets, Apache AH-64 attack helicopters, and the notorious bunker-buster bombs,” the activists went on.

The activist group also noted that CUNY has holdings in GEO Group and CoreCivic, private contractors who operate immigration jails including Delaney Hall in Newark, New Jersey. These corporations “profit from prison labor, ICE detention, deportations, and surveillance,” Mullin said in her speech.

“Even as CUNY management claims to support immigrant students, it has invested the funds of our public university in terrorizing their communities and detaining them and their families,” Mullin added.

She then called for CUNY to respond to the needs of the diverse community it serves.

“We shouldn’t have had to fight for this. This is a public institution. This is the so-called ‘People’s University,’” Mullin said.

Veronica Salama of the New York Civil Liberties Union, which represented the student activists in the legal fight, noted in a press release in August that investment records disclosure “is a basic responsibility and function of a public institution.”

CUNY is the largest urban public university in the country. It now joins the only other U.S. universities that have disclosed their investments in companies complicit in …

title: [Manresa] Propuestas para prevenir las violencias (al hilo del asesinato de Carles, la criminalización racista en redes y la detención de sus asesinos)
content:
ALB. Noticias-

 A continuación traducimos el texto de A l'Aguait de Manresa, campaña que trata sobre la seguridad desde un punto de vista comunitario, a fin de combatir la histeria securitarista que invade la sociedad cada verano, gracias a noticias y sucesos desagradables que tienen que ver con actos delincuenciales y criminales. Esta vez el suceso ha escalado de gravedad, habiendo un

asesinato

. De aquí se lanzó una amplia campaña por redes sociales criminalizando a todos los jóvenes de origen marroquí de la ciudad. La extrema derecha agitó todo lo que pudo hasta que apareció uno de los supuestos perpetradores, que es de origen catalán. Dejando a un lado que se les cayera el argumento, la ultraderecha utiliza estos sucesos de forma habitual y la sociedad va exigiendo medidas "duras", policiales y represivas, antes que luchar contra las causas sociales primeras que originan estas bombas de relojería adolescente. Así pues, el llamdo "Movimento Popular de Manresa" se movilizó y presentó su propuesta, que os la copiamos aquí debajo: 


El orginal, en catalán

. 


Desde A l'aguait, proceso popular de seguridad comunitaria en Manresa y desde el Movimiento Popular de la ciudad,

asumimos nuestra responsabilidad

, como colectivos que trabajamos de forma comunitaria en la ciudad,

de aportar análisis y propuestas útiles

, que nos permitan pasar de la legítima indignación y la tristeza a trabajar por una ciudad

sin violencias, discriminaciones ni desigualdad

.


Estas políticas públicas y comunitarias, divididas en tres fases, surgen del trabajo que llevamos a cabo desde hace más de una década en las calles de Manresa, y del apoyo y las conversaciones con educadoras y expertas en ámbitos como la intervención con jóvenes, la educación y el trabajo social, las drogodependencias, la salud mental y la justicia restaurativa o la violencia juvenil. Están también basadas en la evidencia criminológica y en aprendizajes recogidos en todo el mundo a la hora de combatir la violencia interpersonal, social y comunitaria, especialmente entre jóvenes y desde los jóvenes.


Como Movimiento Popular,

nos preocupa el aumento de las violencias sociales, de los discursos de odio y de la deshumanización en los últimos años

, que sin duda están generando consecuencias materiales, en forma de más exclusión, una peor convivencia y un aumento del miedo entre la ciudadanía.

Un miedo que puede afectar a cómo las manresanas ocupan el espacio público

 y, por tanto, a la cohesión social, y dar alas a aquellos que se aprovechan y arañan votos deformando y distorsionando la realidad para hacernos maleables.

 En Manresa hay violencias que debemos combatir y transformar, aunque sea una ciudad segura.

Del mismo modo que confrontamos la violencia institucional, tampoco podemos ni queremos aceptar que haya personas que son víctimas directas de violencias en nuestra ciudad.


Es necesario, pues, poder

pensar serenamente qué está pasando

, cuál es el alcance de la problemática, cuáles son sus causas y, por tanto, todas las dimensiones que hay que abordar

para prevenir y trabajar en posibles soluciones

. Si algo queda claro, y solo hay que ver lo que ha pasado en otros momentos y contextos, es que abordar la violencia social y comunitaria como una problemática únicamente de seguridad, clamando ciegamente por endurecer uno de los códigos penales más duros de Europa, ni es útil ni ha sido una solución para reducir estas violencias, que tienen múltiples causas.


En el centro, tienen que haber políticas que rompan con las viejas recetas de siempre, que no han sido útiles para disipar la sensación de miedo. Y que no han reducido ni la desigualdad económica, ni la exclusión social, ni la segregación racial, el machismo y la LGTBIfobia, las adicciones y el sufrimiento psíquico o la infravivienda, que siguen creciendo y generando un caldo de cultivo que es imposible de atender desde el punitivismo.


Al mismo tiempo, es urgente incorporar a cualquier análisis la dimensión de género, especialmente en lo que respecta a los mandatos de masculinidad hegemónica que recaen sobre los chicos. author: Unknown
title: Uygur: We are prepared to bear our pain for peace
content:
Families who were unable for years to commemorate their children and siblings lost in the Kurdish Freedom Struggle because of intense state repression are now remembering them at condolence gatherings held across Kurdistan and Turkey. At commemorations organised in Istanbul under the leadership of the Association for Assistance, Solidarity, Unity and Culture for Families Who Lost Relatives in the Cradle of Civilisations (MEBYA-DER), the tears shed and laments sung by mothers are as heartbreaking as the life stories left behind by the guerrillas. At a condolence gathering in Gülsuyu, Maltepe, photographs of three siblings from the Uygur family stood side by side. Ali Uygur spoke to ANF about his siblings Yaşar, Yadigar and Abdulkadir Uygur, who were martyred at different times and in different places.


He could not accept the racist abuse and torture during an ID check


Ali Uygur said his older brother Yaşar was the first member of the family to join the Kurdish Freedom Movement. Explaining that the family comes from the village of Barman in Savur (Stewrê), Mardin (Mêrdîn), Uygur said: “Our family first became acquainted with the movement through my brother. After finishing high school, he was preparing to study mechanical engineering, but financial difficulties forced him to go to Istanbul to work. During an identity check there, police officers saw that he was registered in Mardin and subjected him to racist insults and torture. Unable to accept this racist attack, my brother joined the movement in 1991. He was only 19 at the time. He crossed from the Serhed region into Xakurkê. His achievements within the guerrilla forces led to him becoming a platoon commander. In 1997, during a withdrawal in Xakurkê, an operation was launched in the area where they were positioned. That day, he and 24 comrades held Lêlikan Hill, a strategic position, until the guerrilla force had withdrawn. They were eventually ordered to withdraw as well. To save his 24 comrades during the retreat, my brother stayed behind until the very end and found himself alone, surrounded by KDP peshmerga forces and Turkish soldiers. He fought there until his last bullet and, rather than be captured alive, detonated the explosive he was carrying and was martyred.”


My sister Yadigar was either tortured to death or died from blood loss


Uygur said that after his brother Yaşar, his sister Yadigar became a target of the state: “In 1994, comrade Şoreş was followed while coming to our home in Mardin, and special operations forces and plainclothes police raided the house. I was six years old at the time. Şoreş resisted during the raid and was martyred there, while my sister was wounded. Uygur said: “The special operations officers stripped her naked, wrapped her in a blanket that had been bought for her dowry and put her in an armoured vehicle. My sister was alive when they put her inside because her hand was moving. But we were later informed that she had died. She was either tortured to death or died from blood loss. I believe the plainclothes officers who came to the house with the special operations forces were members of the Gendarmerie Intelligence and Counter-Terrorism (JITEM), because the same team had previously raided homes in Kızıltepe, Mardin, and devastated families like ours.”


They buried her with comrade Şoreş without performing any religious rites


Uygur said: “At first, we could not locate my sister’s grave. We later learned that she had been buried together with her comrade Şoreş in the cemetery where Mehmet Sincar, the murdered Mardin MP for the Democracy Party (DEP), was buried, without any religious rites being performed. They dug the ground with an excavator and placed both of them in the same grave. They are still buried together in that cemetery.”


My 14-year-old brother Kadir was tortured for two months, my mother gave birth in custody


Uygur said that on the day his wounded sister was taken away in an armoured vehicle, his brother Abdülkadir, who was only 14 at the time, and his pregnant mother were also detained and subjected to torture. He noted that his younger sister was born while their mother was in custody. His mother was released after giving birth, while his brother Kadir Uygur, still a child, was subjected to severe torture. Uygur also said: “My brother Abdülkadir was held by them for around two months. The counter-guerrilla had a headquarters in Mardin, and he was subjected to severe torture there. He could not even …

author: By L. Cam Anderson, Contributor
title: The White Supremacist Pastor in Jake Lang’s Shadow
content:
Minneapolis, MN — On

Aug. 22

, far-right provocateur Edward Jacob “Jake” Lang arrived in front of Minneapolis City Hall in the bed of a black Honda Ridgeline followed by a white SUV occupied by private security guards Lang hired for display.


Lang, who was accompanied by six others in the back of the truck, was here for his “N-word march” – spelled out in whole on the event’s flyer – protesting against the verdict reached weeks earlier against Rochester resident Shiloh Hendrix for calling an 8-year-old boy the slur at a playground last year.


As the crowd of counter-protesters surrounded the truck to drown out whatever Lang planned on shouting into his megaphone, a man in a camouflage balaclava and sunglasses whipped out his phone and began recording. Moments later, a man dressed as Spider-Man climbed over the cab of the truck and lunged at Lang, striking him several times in the face.


Matthew Oduguwa,

one of Lang’s security guards

, was busy pepper spraying peaceful protesters and press when he noticed this, turning back to the truck to grab at Spider-Man, wrenching him off of Lang and dragging him over the top of the balaclava-wearing man, who fell overboard head-first onto the sidewalk below.


Joel Tenney, wearing a camouflage balaclava, falling off of the truck beneath the counter-protester dressed as Spider-Man.


The man, whose real identity was pastor Joel Tenney of Tiffin, Iowa, quickly scurried away through the cloud of noxious chemicals that Oduguwa and another security guard named Steve Major hosed the crowd down with, disappearing somewhere behind the white SUV.


“Bear spray hits different,” Tenney posted to his Instagram story later with a selfie across the street from City Hall, the balaclava peeled back to reveal ruby-red skin and a stream of snot running from his nose, coating his upper-lip. “At least I took down gay spiderman when he started throwing hands at Jake, busted my nose throwing him to the concrete tho [

sic

].”


The post from Joel Tenney’s Instagram story, where he goes by “honorablecrusader” (Instagram).


Tenney, who runs Alpha Pneuma Ministries, was not among the seven people arrested by police later in the day, apparently not accompanying Lang and the others as they fled the scene. 


Hennepin County at first charged the seven with probable cause riot, only to renege on the charges after it was revealed that the n-word march was coordinated with the Minneapolis Police Department in advance – something that was very obvious to those at the scene watching the police work hand in hand with the hired security. 


After a few days over the weekend and 36 hours of probable cause hold, the jail released all but Lang, who was awaiting extradition to Texas after the arrest violated his bond in the Lone Star State. Like the initial charges, that fell through as well, and Lang was ultimately released with zero consequences.


Photos of Joel Tenney with Donald Trump (left) and JD Vance (right). In the photo with JD Vance, Tenney is photographed wearing a hat representing his role as a caucus captain in Iowa (Instagram).


Of all of the men who accompanied Lang on his racial slur-themed event, Tenney has one of the largest national profiles. Like Lang, the Armenia-obsessed MAGA pastor from Iowa is an unabashed white supremacist – a term Tenney cloaks with euphemisms – and dedicates much of his public activism to transforming the United States into a Christian theocracy.


In the lead-up to the 2024 presidential election, in December 2023, Tenney led an Iowa Trump rally in prayer as an official speaker. Before praying over the ravenous multitude, he made the case that re-electing “President Trump for the third time” would result in punishment for people who promote “evil” in the country.


“This election is part of a spiritual battle,” Tenney said. “There are demonic forces at play. But judgement is coming.”


This is not such an extreme jump for Tenney, who has directly compared Trump to Jesus Christ in the past by referring to the president as “God’s anointed man.”


Joel Tenney speaking at a Trump rally in Iowa in 2023 (YouTube).


Tenney appeared on a small podcast in July, where the hosts thanked him for connecting them with Lang for an episode that appears to be missing from their uploads.

author: Kimberly Mabaso
title: Papers, Please: Canon Collins 2026 Essay Shortlisted Finalist
content:
This piece was a shortlisted finalist for the

Canon Collins 2026 essay competition

. The annual competition invites essays that demonstrate thought leadership and offer fresh perspectives on issues affecting southern Africa.


Some of my earliest memories are not of places but of words.


One of those words was

kwerekwere

.


I heard it long before I understood it. It drifted through school corridors and playground conversations, sometimes wrapped in laughter, sometimes sharpened into an insult. As a child, I knew nothing about immigration policies, borders or xenophobia. I only knew that whenever the word was directed at me, it carried a message that was impossible to misunderstand, it said to me “you are not one of us”.


I was two years old when my family moved from Zimbabwe to South Africa. South Africa is where I learned to read and write, where I made friends, where I attended school and imagined a future for myself. It is the country whose streets, accents and seasons shaped my understanding of the world. It is, for all practical purposes, home. Yet there were moments growing up when none of that seemed to matter as much as the place printed on a birth certificate. The older I became, the more I realised that borders do not always exist where we think they do. We imagine borders as fences, checkpoints and lines drawn across maps, but the most enduring borders are often invisible. They appear in conversations. They reveal themselves in assumptions. They emerge when someone asks where you are really from, as though your first answer could not possibly be enough. They surface whenever a person is reduced to their nationality before they are recognised as a human being.


My earliest encounter with this reality came when I was six years old. Xenophobic violence had erupted in parts of South Africa. Years later, newspapers would describe the attacks in terms of immigration, politics and public unrest. My memory is much simpler. I remember sleeping at the beach with my family because it felt safer than sleeping at home. I remember the uneasiness of the adults around me and the strange awareness that something had changed, even if I could not yet understand what it was. Children rarely understand the reasons behind fear, they simply absorb it. Looking back, what unsettles me most is not the violence itself but the ideas that made it possible. Violence does not begin with burning shops or broken windows. By the time those things happen, something deeper has already taken root. It begins in the stories people tell about who belongs and who does not. It grows whenever human beings are transformed into problems to be solved rather than neighbours to be known.


In recent years, South Africa has once again witnessed a rise in anti-immigrant sentiment. Foreign nationals are routinely blamed for unemployment, crime and failing public services. Faced with complex social and economic challenges, it is often easier to point to visible outsiders than to confront more difficult realities. Yet what I find particularly striking is how little legality seems to matter. Public debates often suggest that the issue is documentation, that hostility is directed only at those who lack the proper papers. Yet lived experience tells a different story. Refugees carrying valid permits, students lawfully enrolled at universities and long-term residents who have spent years contributing to their communities often find themselves subjected to the same suspicion. Recent anti-immigrant campaigns and protests have only reinforced this reality, demonstrating how quickly legal status can become irrelevant once a person is marked as an outsider.  The issue, it seems, is no longer legality. The issue is belonging.


When I was younger, I believed documents had power. Adults treated them as though they did. Passports were carefully stored. Permits were renewed. Birth certificates were tucked away in drawers and folders. Documents opened doors, crossed borders and settled questions. Or so I thought. As I grew older, I realised that documents answer only certain kinds of questions. They can tell people where you were born. They can confirm your legal status. They can prove that you are permitted to be somewhere. What they cannot do is convince someone that you belong. That lesson reveals itself in small moments: a question asked with just enough suspicion to make you uncomfortable, a joke that everyone else laughs at, the pause that follows your …

content:
Το Σάββατο 5/9 στις 18:00, ενόψει των εγκαινίων της 90ης ΔΕΘ, συνδικάτα, εργατικά σωματεία, φοιτητικοί σύλλογοι, οργανώσεις και συλλογικότητες από όλη τη χώρα καλούν σε μαζικές συγκεντρώσεις στο κέντρο της πόλης, για να διαδηλώσουν με κεντρικό σύνθημα τους αγώνες για ζωή, ελευθερία και αξιοπρέπεια, ενάντια στον εργασιακό μεσαίωνα, στην κοινωνική – οικονομική εξαθλίωση, τους πολέμους και τις δολοφονικές πολιτικές του καπιταλιστικού συστήματος.


Τα κύρια αιτήματα των κινητοποιήσεων είναι η κατάργηση των αντεργατικών νόμων, η θέσπιση συλλογικών συμβάσεων εργασίας με αξιοπρεπείς μισθούς, το τέλος στον πληθωρισμό, στην ανασφάλεια και στην στεγαστική κρίση, αλλά και η παύση κάθε συμμετοχής του ελληνικού κράτους στη γενοκτονία των παλαιστινίων και στις νέες πολεμικές καμπάνιες και συμφωνίες με το Ισραήλ και το ΝΑΤΟ.


Τα καλέσματα λαμβάνουν χώρα σε τέσσερις διαφορετικές τοποθεσίες στο κέντρο της πόλης: Στην Καμάρα όπου καλούν πρωτοβάθμια σωματεία, ταξικές και φοιτητικές πρωτοβουλίες, οργανώσεις και συλλογικότητες. Στο Άγαλμα Βενιζέλου καλούν οι ΓΣΕΕ, ΑΔΕΔΥ και το Εργατοϋπαλληλικό Κέντρο Θεσσαλονίκης. Στην πλατεία ΧΑΝΘ (17.30) το ΠΑΜΕ. Στην Εγνατία και Αγία Σοφία η ΟΚΔΕ.


Παράλληλα σωματεία και εργατικές πρωτοβουλίες οργανώνουν μετακινήσεις από διάφορα σημεία της χώρας με λεωφορεία, με σκοπό την διευκόλυνση στη μεταφορά των διαδηλωτών στη Θεσσαλονίκη ενόψει των κινητοποιήσεων. Παρακάτω ακολουθούν τα ραντεβού των μετακινήσεων ανά πόλη και αναλυτικά τα καλέσματα των διαδηλώσεων.

title: İHD 2025 Yılı Hak İhlalleri Raporu: Sandığa darbe, sokağa yumruk
content:
Eylem Nazlıer [email protected]

İnsan Hakları Derneği’nin (İHD) basından ve açık kaynaklardan derlediği bilgilerle hazırladığı 2025 Yılı Hak İhlalleri Raporu, Kürt sorununda çatışmalı süreç geride kalsa da birçok temel alanda insan hakları ihlallerinin tüm ağırlıyla varlığını sürdürdüğünü ortaya koydu. Raporda, “barış ortamını besleyip güçlendirecek yeterli demokratik adımların atılmaması, üstelik her türlü toplumsal tepkiyi yargı kılıcı ve kolluk sopasıyla bastırmayı düstur edinen yönetim anlayışının devam etmesi yine pek çok temel hakkın ihlaline yol açtı” tespitinde bulunuldu.

Rapora göre, 2025 yılında en çok hak ihlali tespit edilen iller sırasıyla İstanbul, Ankara, İzmir, Bursa, Van, Antalya, Diyarbakır, Mersin, Kocaeli ve Şırnak oldu. Nüfusa oranla en sık hak ihlali tespit edilen illerin başını ise Tunceli (Dersim) çekti. Onu sırasıyla Erzincan, Bolu, Kırşehir, Şırnak, Van, Ankara, İstanbul, Elazığ ve Iğdır takip etti.

Rapora göre, yaşam hakkına yönelik ihlaller sonucu en az 2.749 kişi hayatını kaybetti, en az 1.112 kişi yaralandı. Yaşam hakkı ihlallerinde başı iş cinayetleri çekti. 2025 yılında en az 2.105 kişi iş cinayetleri sonucu yaşamını yitirdi. Böylece 2016-2015 yılları arasında, 10 yılda iş cinayetleri sonucu ölen kişi sayısı 20.009 kişiye ulaştı. 2025’in ekonomik kriz ve MESEM vb. uygulamalarla çocuk işçiliğinde yaşanan kitleselleşmenin sonuçlarına da dikkat çekilen raporda, 26’sı 14 yaş ve altı, en az 94 çocuğun iş cinayetlerinde hayatını kaybettiği aktarıldı.

Rapora göre, Cumhurbaşkanı Erdoğan’ın “Aile Yılı” ilan ettiği 2025 yılında, kadınlar ve çocuklar yine erkek şiddetinin hedefi oldular. Her gün en az bir kadın ya da çocuk erkek şiddeti sonucu yaşamını yitirdi. Kadınlar en çok iktidarca konumlandırıldıkları “evde” şiddete maruz kalırken, bu şiddetin faili de yine eski/yeni eşler, partnerler ile baba, kardeş, damat gibi erkek aile fertleriydi.

Raporda, İHD’nin 1991 yılından bu yana yaptığı çalışmalara dayanılarak, Kürt sorununda çatışmalı süreç nedeniyle en az 36.479 kişinin yaşamını yitirdiği aktarıldı. İHD’nin verilerine göre, 25 yıllık bu süreçte 27.025 kişinin doğrudan operasyon ve çatışmalarda, 9.454 kişinin ise çatışmalı süreçle bağlantılı diğer saldırı ve yaşam hakkı ihlalleri sonucu hayatını kaybetti.

Rapora 2025 yılında, en az 159 kişi resmi ihmal ve denetimsizlik sonucu hayatını kaybetti. Deprem, sel vb. doğa olayları sonucu en az 1 kişi öldü, en az 180 kişi yaralandı. Bolu’da otel yangınında 34’ü çocuk, toplam 78 kişi yaşamını yitirdi. Orman yangınlarında 10 kişi yaşamını yitirdi. Kolluk güçlerine ait araçların karıştığı kazalar sonucu 20’si asker, 7’si mülteci, 1’i çocuk en az 29 kişi yaşamını yitirdi.

Ayrıca, kolluk güçlerinin silah kullanma yetkisini ihlal etmesi sonucu en az 3 kişi yaşamını yitirdi, en az 5 kişi yaralandı.

2025 yılında politik nedenler ya da ırkçı, ayrımcı, fobik saiklerle gerçekleştirilen en az 43 fiziksel ya da silahlı saldırı basına yansıdı. Bu saldırılarla en az 148 kişi doğrudan hedef alınırken, bu saldırılarda en az 15 kişi yaşamını yitirdi, en az 52 kişi yaralandı.

En az 9 gazeteci saldırıya uğradı. Hakan Tosun hayatını kaybetti. Dönemin CHP Genel Bşk. Özgür Özel fiziksel saldırıya uğradı. IŞİD ile ilişkili 2 saldırıda, en az 6 polis ve 6 silahlı örgüt militanı yaşamını yitirdi. En az 5 fobik saldırı tespit edildi. 1 trans kadın öldürüldü. 8 ırkçı saldırıda en az 14 kişi yaralandı. 12 yaşındaki mülteci çocuk evinde uğradığı saldırı sonucu öldürüldü. Fındıklı Belediye Başkanı saldırıya uğradı.

2025 yılında en az 1842 kişi işkence ve diğer kötü muamele niteliğindeki uygulamalara maruz kaldı.

Ankara’da gözaltında işkence gördüğü iddia edilen Musa Nargüner, tedavi gördüğü hastanede yaşamını yitirdi. 1’i geri gönderme merkezlerinde en az 90 kişi resmi gözaltı yerlerinde işkence ve kötü muameleye maruz kaldı. 1493’ü toplantı ve gösterilere yönelik kolluk müdahalelerinde olmak üzere, en az 1592 kişi resmi gözaltı yerleri dışında işkence ve kötü muameleye maruz kaldı. En az 185 mahpus hapishanelerde işkence ve kötü muameleye maruz bırakıldı.

2024 yerel seçimlerinden 2025 yılı sonuna kadar 27 belediye başkanı görevden uzaklaştırıldı, 13 belediyeye kayyum atandı. 16 belediye başkanı tutuklandı.

author: Emma Anderson
title: Support Is Growing in the Push to Recognize Gender Apartheid as a Crime Against Humanity
content:
The movement for the rights and freedom of Afghan women and girls is picking up momentum in the halls of the United Nations. Feminist Majority Foundation (FMF) and other feminist civil society leaders and activists are currently engaged in the historic process of negotiations for a crimes against humanity treaty, which will provide a formal mechanism for recognizing, codifying, and holding perpetrators accountable for a suite of atrocities that have fallen through the gaps of existing international laws for decades. Crucially, the negotiations for this treaty provide a window for feminists to ensure that all forms of gender-based persecution are defined, recognized, and punished for what they are: global atrocities and systematic violence permeating all levels of society.

On July 28, the UN released an updated version of the draft articles, which includes amendments and additions that ensure gender apartheid is recognized throughout the text. On June 4, Australia, Afghanistan (UN mission), Iceland, Mexico, Timor-Leste, Uruguay, and Spain agreed to include gender apartheid in their amendments; the draft released in July reflects these commitments in writing. These 7 states join Austria, Portugal, Malta, Philippines, Chile, Brazil and Luxembourg as champions in the global fight for the rights and dignity of Afghan women and girls living under the oppressive Taliban regime.

There were also multiple additions and amendments to include forced marriage as its own category, put forward by several states: Canada, the Netherlands, Sierra Leone, Germany, Belgium, Colombia, the UK, Andorra, Cyprus, Ukraine, and Poland, in addition to states also proposing to include gender apartheid. This same group of states, in addition to the Nordic states, also proposed to expand the definition of sexual violence to cover specific types of reproductive violence, like forced sterilization and forced birth.

The show of support by some states for forced marriage and reproductive violence, while stopping short of “gender apartheid,” presents an opportunity for feminist organizations to keep advocating for the full breadth of gender-based oppression to be appropriately recognized by the UN. At FMF, we call on these states to embrace this fight to the fullest extent. The totality of Afghan women and girls’ oppression needs to be unequivocally condemned by the international community in all its forms.

FMF will continue to push for full recognition of gender apartheid as the UN continues the long process of creating a new legal instrument for identifying and punishing crimes against humanity. FMF’s advocacy on this issue draws from the real voices and leadership of women and girls in Afghanistan, and we echo their calls for a refusal to recognize or normalize the Taliban.

Countries that have demonstrated solidarity and leadership in this urgent fight for humanity and freedom are setting an important example. This is a critical moment to engage more partners and representatives at the UN and beyond, build on this momentum, and advance a Crimes Against Humanity Convention that recognizes gender apartheid and accurately reflects the voices, experiences, and lives of women and girls in Afghanistan.

author: Mike Ludwig
title: Trump Wants “Model Cities” With High-Tech Police. New Orleans Just Said “No.”
content:
New Orleans is the latest to refuse a $300 million grant program that critics say would build Trump’s police state.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

After taking a “serious look” at applying for federal funding under the Trump administration’s Model Cities Initiative, the city leaders of cash-strapped New Orleans announced on August 31 that they will not apply for the controversial grant program.

The $300 million grant program for cities and local governments of more than 100,000 people offers to pay for high-tech policing and public safety infrastructure in exchange for local officials complying with federal mass deportation efforts, among other priorities. Critics say the initiative is the tip of the spear for deploying mass surveillance tech and indulging the authoritarian impulses of President Donald Trump, who has filled the streets of multiple cities with violent federal immigration agents and, in several cases, armed federal troops.

New Orleans is a majority-Black city steeped in civil rights history, and activists have been ringing alarm bells for weeks as Mayor Helena Moreno and other city leaders mulled over whether to apply for the grant amid pressure from the state’s GOP-controlled government to address an ongoing budget crisis.

Edith Romero, an organizer in New Orleans with the privacy group Eye on Surveillance, is grateful that local advocates and residents voiced their opposition and pushed the city away from applying for the grant.

“The Model Cities Initiative is a Justice Department grant program that comes with serious strings attached, including the sharing of immigration information between state, federal and local agencies,” Romero told Truthout in an email. “This means surveillance for Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to separate families and terrorize our communities.”

According to the Justice Department, one of the policy “blueprints” for the Model Cities Initiative is President Donald Trump’s law enforcement surge in Memphis, Tennessee — another Democratic-led, majority-Black city in a GOP-controlled state. Launched about a year ago and involving 13 federal agencies as well as state and local law enforcement, the surge of what the White House calls “hypervigilant policing” in Memphis is still in effect. Residents and civil rights groups describe the surge as a racist and militarized federal “assault” and “occupation” and a new form of colonialism.

While the administration claims the Memphis task force is focused on “arresting violent criminals … seizing firearms, and locating missing children,” the operation, in actuality, was part of an aggressive immigration sweep. Officers have made large numbers of traffic stops to check for immigration status and have engaged in clearly documented racial profiling, according to local officials.

In Memphis, the Trump administration’s multi-agency Memphis Safe Task Force has been accused of terrorizing Black and Brown neighborhoods and retaliating against locals who attempt to record interactions with law enforcement on their phones in violation of their First Amendment rights, according to a lawsuit filed in May on behalf of four Memphis residents by the American Civil Liberties Union.

Federal troops and officers with the task force shot and killed at least four Black men in Memphis over a two-month period this summer. In at least two of the cases, autopsies and surveillance video footage cast doubt on initial claims by law enforcement that the victims pointed firearms at officers.

A National Guard team on the task force fatally shot 20-year-old Tyrin Johnson in the back as he was running away in July. Johnson’s family is calling for the guardsmen responsible to be criminally charged. Meanwhile, in New Orleans, the National Guard just finished its latest deployment to the historic French Quarter, where federal troops have mingled among tourists for the past eight months.

In a statement on August 31, New Orleans Deputy Mayor of Public Safety Michael Harrison cited unspecified questions about “legal issues” as he said that the city had decided against applying for the Model Cities Initiative. New Orleans joined Charlotte, North Carolina, and Billings, Montana, in publicly announcing that an application for Model Cities would not be submitted before the deadline passed on …

title: Έκτακτη εκδήλωση & συζήτηση: Κούρδος πολιτικός πρόσφυγας κινδυνεύει με απέλαση πίσω στην Τουρκία
content:
Σύνδεσμος δημοσίευσης:

Έκτακτη εκδήλωση & συζήτηση: Κούρδος πολιτικός πρόσφυγας κινδυνεύει με απέλαση πίσω στην Τουρκία


Solidarity with Migrants


ΕΚΤΑΚΤΗ ΕΚΔΗΛΩΣΗ-ΣΥΖΗΤΗΣΗ


Την Πέμπτη 10/9 στις 19:30 στο συλλογικό καφέ (κιόσκι) της Κοινότητας Κατειλημμένων Προσφυγικών.


Ο Soner Inanç, Κούρδος πολιτικός αγωνιστής για τα εργατικά δικαιώματα και τις δημοκρατικές ελευθερίες διανύει την 16η μέρα απεργίας πείνας σε καθεστώς κράτησης ενώ κινδυνεύει με άμεση απέλαση λόγω της ενδεχόμενης απόρριψης της αίτησής του για άσυλο. O πολιτικός πρόσφυγας Soner Inanç αναγκάστηκε να εγκαταλείψει την Τουρκία καθώς έχει στοχοποιηθεί για τη δράση του από το τουρκικό κράτος και ήδη έχει φυλακιστεί στο παρελθόν για τη συμμετοχή του στο κίνημα του Gezi Park.


Μετά την απορριπτική απόφαση ως προς το αρχικό αίτημα ασύλου του, Soner Inanç κατέθεσε αίτημα ακύρωσης και ακολούθησε όλες τις σχετικές διαδικασίες. Τέλη Ιουλίου, συνελήφθη και βρέθηκε σε καθεστώς διοικητικής κράτησης στο ΑΤ Λαυρίου. Ένα μήνα μετά, μεταφέρθηκε στη Θεσσαλονίκη με σκοπό την απέλαση του. Λίγες μέρες πριν, του γνωστοποιήθηκε καταδίκη στην Τουρκία απλώς και μόνο για τη συμμετοχή του στις διαδηλώσεις του κινήματος για το Gezi Park. Επί τη βάση της καταδικαστικής αυτής απόφασης κατέθεσε μεταγενέστερο αίτημα ασύλου και μπλόκαρε την απέλαση. Αυτήν την στιγμή κρατείται προσωρινά στο κλειστό στρατόπεδο (ΠΡΟΚΕΚΑ) Δράμας. Αν απελαθεί, κινδυνεύει η ζωή του με βασανιστήρια στο καθεστώς των τουρκικών φυλακών.


Ο Soner Inanç από την αρχή της γνωστοποίησης της απέλασης στην Τουρκία ξεκίνησε απεργία πείνας με αίτημα την αναγνώριση πολιτικού ασύλου και την απελευθέρωσή του. Διανύοντας πλέον την 16η ημέρα απεργίας πείνας, η αστυνομία αρνείται να δεχτεί το αίτημα των γιατρών που τον παρακολουθούν να λάβει βιταμίνες, γεγονός που θέτει σε κίνδυνο τη ζωή του άμεσα. Με λίγα λόγια, το ελληνικό κράτος οδηγεί στο θάνατο έναν πολιτικά διωκόμενο πρόσφυγα από το τουρκικό κράτος αρνούμενο μέχρι και τη στοιχειώδη ιατρική υποστήριξη του.


Το μεταγενέστερο αίτημα του κρίθηκε, λανθασμένα, απαράδεκτο σήμερα και θα ασκηθεί προσφυγή.


Ως Solidarity with Migrants, γνωρίσαμε τον Soner στο στρατόπεδο προσφύγων Οινοφύτων όπου πάντα προσπαθούσε με όλα τα δυνατά μέσα να υποστηρίζει τα δικαιώματα όλων των προσφύγων με μια βαθιά διεθνιστική προσήλωση.


Αυτή τη στιγμή η ζωή του Soner κινδυνεύει με ευθύνη του αρμόδιων θεσμών και μηχανισμών του ελληνικού κράτους, καθώς δεν αποδέχονται το στοιχειώδες αίτημα ιατρικής υποστήριξης στην απεργία πείνας και ταυτόχρονα συνεχίζουν να καταστρατηγούν το δικαίωμα του στο πολιτικό άσυλο οδηγώντας σε απέλαση στην Τουρκία για φυλάκιση με άμεσο κίνδυνο για τη ζωή του.


Στηρίζουμε σε όλα τα επίπεδα τον αγώνα για άμεση απελευθέρωση και απόδοση πολιτικού ασύλου.


Αλληλεγγύη στον Soner Inanç!


***


ACİL ÇAĞRILI ETKİNLİK – TARTIŞMA


10 Eylül Perşembe günü saat 19:30’da, İşgal Edilmiş Mülteci Evleri (Prosfygika) kolektif kafesinde (Kioski) buluşuyoruz.


Soner İnanç, işçi hakları ve demokratik özgürlükler için mücadele eden bir Kürt aktivist, gözaltında 16. gününe giren açlık grevini sürdürüyor ve siyasi sığınma başvurusunun reddedilmesi ihtimalinden dolayı halen sınır dışı edilme tehlikesiyle karşı karşıya. Politik mülteci Soner İnanç, faaliyetleri nedeniyle Türk devleti tarafından hedef alındığı için Türkiye’yi terk etmek zorunda kaldı; daha önce de Gezi Parkı direnişine katıldığı için hapiste kalmıştı.


İlk sığınma talebinin reddedilmesinin ardından Soner İnanç, itiraz davası açtı ve ilgili tüm prosedürleri takip etti. O dönemde, Lavrio Emniyet Müdürlüğü’nde idari olarak gözaltında tutuluyordu ve aynı zamanda Türkiye’de Gezi Parkı direnişindeki protestolarına katıldığı için hakkında bir mahkumiyet kararı çıkmıştı. Buna rağmen Yunan polisinin tarafından deport amacıyla Selanik’e nakledildi. Şu anda Drama’daki kapalı askeri kampta (PROKEKA) geçici olarak tutulmaktadır. Sınır dışı edilirse, Türkiye’de işkence ve yeniden tutuklanma tehlikesiyle karşı karşıya kalacaktır.


Soner İnanç, Türkiye’ye sınır dışı edileceğinin bildirilmesinden itibaren, siyasi sığınma hakkının tanınması ve serbest bırakılması talebiyle açlık grevine başladı. Açlık grevinin 16. gününe girerken, polis, onu takip eden doktorların vitamin alması yönündeki talebini reddediyor ve bu durum, onun hayatını doğrudan tehlikeye atıyor. author: Simon Childs
title: Anti-Migrant Protesters Invade Hotel of Pakistani Cricket Team
content:
Protesters banged on the bedroom doors of Portsmouth’s Marriott hotel on Tuesday night, believing they had found a group of migrants to harass. However, they went home after discovering they were protesting a visiting Pakistani cricket team.


Protesters reportedly reached the floor the professional athletes were staying on, believing the four-star hotel was being used to house asylum seekers. 


The chief operating officer of the Pakistan Cricket Board, Sumair Syed, told the BBC the team reported people “knocking on their doors”, but the cricketers “behaved responsibly and didn’t escalate the situation” he said. 


Councillor George Madgwick, the leader of Reform UK in Hampshire was in attendance.


In a since deleted Facebook post he wrote: “A number of concerned local residents spotted what they believed to be migrants going into the Marriott hotel.


“I visited the manager and the hotel explained it was a Pakistani Cricket team staying. The cricket team coach came to speak to me personally and I saw proof (hotel were happy to provide).”


Madgwick claimed he spoke directly to the crowd of “40/50 people” who he said “respectfully accepted” that the guests weren’t asylum seekers and left within five minutes. 


The incident comes as Hampshire Police investigate reports of assaults and criminal damage on Sunday night, when far-right activist ‘Danny Tommo’ led hundreds of people to Portsmouth harbour. The crowd, some of whom were wearing masks, confronted riot police in order to stop the arrival of 120 people who had been travelling to the UK in a single dinghy.


Hampshire Police said no offences were committed on Tuesday, and the crowd dispersed at around 9pm.


Madgwick, who has been conducting an extended media round defending the anti-migrant protest on Sunday night, appeared to take credit. “I’m glad I could do my bit to help the situation and stop tensions rising,” he said on Facebook. 


“The hotel manager was very thankful and actually was sympathetic to the local issues at the moment but just wanted her guests not to have to worry, which is fair enough.”


In a caustic post on Facebook, Portsmouth Stand Up to Racism said Madgwick “fell short of claiming that he deserved the Nobel Peace prize for his mediation skills.”


The group added: “Allowing racists to mobilise like this every time they become suspicious of any group of non-white people in Portsmouth is extremely dangerous. It is racism in action and it has to stop.”


The Portsmouth Marriott hotel has been approached for comment.


This is not the first time migrant-mania has led to confusion. Last year, Reform UK politician Ryan Coogan, shared a picture of some people getting out of a minibus in Cromer and asked, “Is this part of another quiet relocation scheme – although these usually happen in the middle of the night?” The image was also circulated on far-right Facebook groups, but it turned out to be a group of young churchgoers on a trip to the seaside.


Anyone who believes that Reform’s anti-migrant stance could improve things for the workers in the UK might be interested in

The Bureau of Investigative Journalism’s (TBIJ) 

 finding that two of Madgwick’s restaurant businesses have been ordered to pay £4,386 to former employees for breaching employment law, by failing to pay holiday and maternity pay. He told TBIJ the rulings were made without the companies having the opportunity to defend the claims.

title: İsviçre 5 çocuklu Özgün ailesini de Türkiye'ye geri göndermek istiyor
content:
İsviçre’de yaklaşık 3 yıldır yaşayan Dilan ve Nihat Özgün ile 5 çocuklarının Türkiye’ye sınır dışı edilmesi girişimi üzerine ailenin ülkedeki yakınları ve dayanışma grupları harekete geçti. Ailenin iltica gerekçesinin yeniden değerlendirilmesi ve sınır dışı kararının durdurulması talebiyle imza kampanyası başlatıldı.


Zürih kantonundaki Oberhalden Finkenried geri gönderme merkezinde kalan Özgün ailesinin verdiği bilgiye göre İsviçre’ye sığınmalarının temelinde Türkiye’de karşı karşıya oldukları siyasi kovuşturmalar var. 


Sınır dışı kararının uygulanması için daha önce merkeze çok sayıda polisin görev aldığı bir operasyon düzenlendi. Dilan Özgün’ün kelepçelenerek merkezden çıkarılmak istendiği, ancak merkezde kalanların ve dayanışmaya gelenlerin müdahalesi üzerine sınır dışı işleminin gerçekleştirilemediği bildirildi.


Beş çocuğun yaşamı artık İsviçre’de


Özgün, operasyonun özellikle çocuklar üzerinde ağır etkisi olduğunu söylüyor.


“Bir anne olarak artık korkusuzca uyumak istiyorum; geceleri, çocuklarımı yanımda olmalarına rağmen, defalarca kontrol etmek istemiyorum” diyen Özgün, çocuklarının İsviçre’deki yaşıtları gibi sınır dışı edilme kaygısı taşımadan yaşayabilmesini istiyor.


Ailenin itirazının önemli bir bölümü beş çocuğun İsviçre’de kurdukları yaşama dayanıyor. 


Özgün, çocuklarının ailelerinin siyasi geçmişinden sorumlu tutulamayacağını belirterek, “Geliş sebebimiz ne kadar politik sebeplerden olsa da çocuklarımızın bunda bir payı yoktu. Çünkü onlar çocuk” diyor.


Ailenin aktardığına göre yaklaşık 3 yıldır İsviçre’de yaşayan çocuklar; eğitimlerini burada sürdürüyor, arkadaşlıkları ve sosyal çevreleri burada kuruluyor.


Özgün, çocukların artık Türkiye’de süren okul ve sosyal yaşamları bulunmadığını belirterek şöyle diyor:


“Çocuklarımın burada bir hayatı var. Arkadaşlarıyla, çevreleriyle birlikte mutlular ve yaşamları artık burada. Türkiye’de bir okul hayatları kalmadı. Bu yüzden bu saatten sonra çocuklarım için burada kalma mücadelesini veriyorum.”


Aile için başlatılan kampanyada da İsviçre makamlarından, yalnızca ebeveynlerin iltica dosyasını değil, çocukların ülkede geçirdikleri süreyi, eğitimlerini, sosyal bağlarını ve sınır dışı edilmelerinin çocuklar üzerindeki etkilerini birlikte değerlendirmeleri isteniyor.


Dilan Özgün çağrısını, “Çocukların sınırları ve statüleri olmamalı” sözleriyle dile getiriyor.


Aynı merkezden gönderilen Yalçınkaya Türkiye’de tutuklandı


Özgün ailesinin sınır dışı edilmesine yönelik kaygıları, aynı geri gönderme merkezinde kalan başka bir Türkiyeli sığınmacının başına gelenlerle daha somut bir boyut kazandı.


Bahar Yalçınkaya, beş yaşındaki çocuğu ve İsviçre’de dünyaya gelen 15 aylık bebeğiyle birlikte 5 Ağustos’ta Oberhalden Finkenried merkezinden alınarak Türkiye’ye sınır dışı edildi.


Avukatının Türkiye’de tutuklanma riski bulunduğu yönünde İsviçre makamlarını uyardığı bildirildi. Buna rağmen sınır dışı edilen Yalçınkaya Türkiye’ye girişinin ardından gözaltına alındı ve ertesi gün “örgüt propagandası yapmak” suçlamasıyla tutuklandı. Suçlamaya sosyal medya paylaşımlarının dayanak yapıldığı bildirildi.


Yalçınkaya 15 aylık bebeğiyle birlikte Bakırköy Kadın Kapalı Cezaevi’ne gönderildi. 


İsviçre'nin iade ettiği Bahar Yalçınkaya Türkiye'de tutuklandı, 15 aylık bebeğiyle cezaevinde


6 Ağustos 2026


Olay, İsviçre makamlarının Türkiye’ye gönderilecek kişilerin karşılaşabilecekleri siyasi ve cezai riskleri değerlendirmede başvuru sahiplerinin durumunu gereken ciddiyette değerlendirip değerlendirmediğine  ilişkin tartışmayı büyüttü.


Uluslararası mülteci hukukunun temel ilkelerinden biri olan geri göndermeme (non-refoulement) ilkesi, kişilerin zulüm riskiyle karşılaşabilecekleri yere gönderilmesini yasaklıyor. İsviçre Devlet Göç Sekreterliği de kişilerin iltica başvurusu reddedilmiş olsa bile sınır dışı kararının İsviçre’nin uluslararası yükümlülüklerine, özellikle 1951 Cenevre Mülteci Sözleşmesi’ne uygun olup olmadığının ayrıca incelenmesi gerektiğini belirtiyor. 


Yalçınkaya’nın sınır dışı edildikten hemen sonra tutuklanması, bu risk değerlendirmesinin uygulamada gereğince yerine getirilip getirilmediği sorusunu gündeme taşıdı. 


İsviçre iltica sistemini hızlandırıyor


Özgün ailesinin dosyası aynı zamanda İsviçre’nin iltica politikasında hızlandırma, erken eleme ve geri gönderme mekanizmalarının ağırlığının arttığı bir döneme denk geldi.

author: Redazione_web
title: Migrazioni, repressione e corsa elettorale. La lezione di Ceuta
content:
La settimana scorsa il governo Meloni ha prolungato di altri 15 giorni la sospensione del trattato di Schengen con lo Stato spagnolo ricevendo, come ovvia contropartita, lo stesso trattamento. Le motivazioni pubbliche e sbandierate sono le solite: contrasto all’immigrazione clandestina, lotta al ‘terrorismo’, ecc. Quelle occulte, per chi le vuole vedere, parlano di rilancio del sovranismo identitario e di tentativo di demolizione di ogni politica immigratoria che non sappia di violenza e sfruttamento intensivo.


La vicenda di Ceuta è stata un’occasione troppo grossa, troppo appetitosa per farsela sfuggire e così; grazie al clima preelettorale già ampiamente arroventato, Meloni e i suoi hanno pensato bene di dar fiato alla grancassa, cercando alleanze a destra e a manca (ognuno ha i volenterosi che si merita) e di mettere sulla graticola il premier Sanchez e il suo governo socialista. Tra i primi a rispondere al loro richiamo la socialdemocratica danese – ovviamente osannata dai ‘giornali’ di Angelucci – e le formazioni dal nazionalismo più becero.


Ma cosa è successo a Ceuta, questo piccolo residuo territoriale (insieme a Melilla) dell’impero coloniale spagnolo in Africa? Il 30 luglio un numero di persone imprecisato ma sicuramente superiore a 60mila, è riuscito a penetrare nella città, soprattutto via mare, credendo che in base ad una sentenza della Corte Suprema spagnola essere a Ceuta equivalesse ad essere in Spagna e quindi nell’Unione europea, potendo così presentare domanda di diritto d’asilo e ottenere una sua valutazione da parte dei tribunali. Ma Ceuta gode di un regime particolare che non contempla l’adesione al trattato di Schengen, poiché non appartiene al territorio metropolitano spagnolo, anche se è sottoposta alle sue leggi e numerose caserme alloggiano nella sua area, come d’altronde a Melilla.


Ancora oggi vi è un rimpallo di responsabilità su chi ha favorito in poche ore questo afflusso ingente in una località che conta abitualmente circa 80mila residenti, creando e vivendo, come si può ben capire, non poche difficoltà.


Inizialmente si è pensato subito alle responsabilità del governo del Marocco – firmatario dei Patti d’Abramo e fedele alleato degli USA – che su istigazione statunitense e israeliana avrebbe operato per mettere in difficoltà Sanchez, allo scopo di punirlo sia per la mancata disponibilità delle basi per l’attacco all’Iran sia per il riconoscimento della Palestina come stato indipendente. Oggi Sanchez scagiona il monarca di Rabat, la sua guardia di frontiera e la sua intelligence da ogni responsabilità e accusa russi, Israele e la destra fascista di avere provocato, con la diffusione a pioggia di fakenews, lo sviluppo di illusioni ed aspettative nelle masse giovanili marocchine e subsahariane desiderose di liberarsi dalle condizioni di repressione, oppressione e sottosviluppo nelle quali sono costrette a vivere sotto il tallone di regimi autocratici, militaristi e patriarcali.


L’operazione, secondo Sanchez, rientra nell’obiettivo congiunto dei suoi attori di sfasciare l’Unione europea, riportandola indietro nel tempo, indebolendola per riconsegnarla agli appetiti delle potenze imperialiste.


Quello che è certo è che l’ondata umana, carica di speranze e di disperazione, nonostante in poco tempo sia stata fortemente ridimensionata con il ritorno in Marocco della maggior parte delle persone, ha fornito agli avvoltoi di turno, ai pennivendoli di regime, a teleMeloni, un’immagine utile alla propaganda più becera fatta di minacce di sostituzione etnica, di barbari alle porte, di terroristi jiadisti e chi più ne ha più ne metta.


Un’immagine prontamente giocata sul tavolo dei rapporti di forza a Bruxelles, cercando di imporre politiche del processo migratorio funzionali alla visione autoritaria e suprematista della destra identitaria. Non è un caso che Sanchez e il suo governo, al netto di tutte le brutture che lo contraddistinguono (vedi la successione di scandali che hanno riguardato membri del governo e della famiglia), sia stato messo al palo proprio per le politiche migratorie messe in atto nel paese, politiche tese alla regolamentazione del ‘mercato del lavoro’ e dei permessi di soggiorno, all’eliminazione del lavoro nero, all’integrazione dei lavoratori e delle lavoratrici immigrate.


Politiche che fanno si che la Spagna sia l’unico paese dell’UE ad avere un tasso di crescita superiore a quello di tutti gli altri. Non che questo sia un dato che ci interessi più di tanto, ma …

title: Committee to be established for Iraq and Kurdistan Region border crossings
content:
The Head of the Iraqi Security Information Office, Seed Meen, announced that a 17-point strategic security agreement had been reached between the Kurdistan Region administration and the Iraqi government.


It was reported that representatives of the security institutions in Hewlêr (Erbil) and Silêmanî (Sulaymaniyah), as well as the head of the Iraqi Counter-Terrorism Service, the head of the Iraqi Border Crossings Authority, and the Chief of Staff of the Peshmerga, were present at the high-level security meeting where the agreement was concluded.


Meen said: “The agreement was reached both to strengthen security in areas of common interest between the Kurdistan Region of Iraq and the Iraqi government, and to increase coordination to prevent remnants of terrorist groups and smugglers from exploiting any geographical gaps.”


Meen added that a committee chaired by the head of the Iraqi Border Crossings Authority had been established, adding that the committee would conduct a comprehensive review of border crossings in the Kurdistan Region and work to close unofficial border crossings.


Emphasizing that Iraq now has influence in the region and that the structure of the Peshmerga forces has been preserved, Seed Meen underlined that the agreement would, at this point, strengthen the role of the Border Guard Forces along the Iraq-Turkey line, with the support of the Peshmerga forces.

author: hsa_oryx
title: One Giant Leap: Stag Jumps Hunt Supporters to Escape the Quantock Staghounds
content:
A terrified stag made a dramatic leap for his life on the 24

th

 August, leaping over hunt supporters who were attempting to prevent him from escaping onto land where the Quantock Staghounds could not follow.


Incredible footage of the hunt and the stag’s subsequent escape – albeit temporary – was captured by

Dorset Borders Hunt Sabs

 and

North Dorset Hunt Sabs.


The stag makes a leap for life, as one of the hunt supporters who had been trying to scare him back ducks for cover. Image credit: Dorset Borders Hunt Sabs.


The chase began early that morning, at around 6am at Upcott Farm, Bicknoller. The stag had been chased from maize fields at Heddon Oak, near Crowcombe, over the Minehead railway line, and through woodland owned by Fountain Forestry, before seeking refuge in a small area of miscanthus grass. 


By 8am the hunt had surrounded the grass, and entered hounds, flushing the stag out into the open.


The stag is flushed out of the miscanthus grass into the open.

Image credit North Dorset Hunt Sabs


The land where the stag emerged adjoined a road. On the opposite side of the road lay safety – land that is out of bounds to the hunt, offering some refuge to the stag.


Hunt supporters had lined the road and attempted to prevent the stag from making his escape.


In the video, you can hear one hunter loudly cracking a whip, whilst others shouted and screamed, in an attempt to frighten the stag back towards the hunt.


But the stag did not turn back.


Wayne Gregory, convicted huntsman for the Vale of Taunton & Banwell Harriers attempts to scare the stag back towards the hunt.

Image credit: Dorset Borders Hunt Sabs.


Instead, he leapt for his life, breaking out directly above four men who were screaming and flailing their arms in an attempt to stop him.


The stag landed on the other side and entered the land beyond the hunt’s reach.


But his respite was short lived…


Other hunt supporters positioned on the far side of the out-of-bounds land, spotted the stag as he emerged on the other side and alerted the huntsman. The hounds were promptly brought around and put straight back on the stag’s scent.


The terrified animal was pursued for 4 hours in total, but managed to escape. 

Image credit North Dorset Hunt Sabs.


They pursued him for a further two hours, before the hunt finally lost the stag completely.


But it isn’t guaranteed that the stag survived the trauma. Extreme fear and distress can bring on a severe condition called capture myopathy in deer. If you have ever witnessed an injured deer at the roadside, the animal can sometimes succumb to this condition, rather than the injuries sustained in a collision.


Organs and muscle damage can occur over a period of hours or even days, with the animal displaying symptoms such as weakness, ataxia (poor muscle control), paralysis, hyperventilation and ultimately death.


Even when a hunt is unsuccessful, it can still result in the animal’s death.


When the stag leapt over the hunt supporters, the front supporter frantically flailing his arms before taking a tumble, was none other than Wayne Gregory, the recently convicted huntsman of the Vale of Taunton & Banwell Harriers.


Gregory pleaded guilty after he was caught illegally hunting a fox during a hunt meet in Chilton Trinity on 26 November 2025. He was filmed by Somerset Hunt Sabs using a drone as he directed the hounds to flush then hunt a fox. Immediately after the trial, he declared to the waiting press and public that he was off to change out of his suit to go hunting with the Quantock Staghounds.


Wayne Gregory, convicted huntsman of the Vale of Taunton and Banwell Harriers, and chief stag-shooer for the Quantock Staghounds.

Image Credit: Somerset Sabs


Gregory’s adaptability to switch which quarry he likes to torment, is proof that ‘trail hunting’ is nothing but a cover for illegal hunting.


The Quantock Staghounds routinely invoke various smokescreens for their activities.

Covert hunt sabs

 attending the first meet of the QSH in 2025 witnessed a laughable speech from a hunt master who claimed that the hunt conducts “Research and Observation” of stags, but also stating that ‘trails may be laid’.


An earlier victim of the QSH taken on 25/09/2025.

Image Credit: HSA


The hunt also invokes the “flushing to guns” smokescreen, and claims to be ‘rescuing a casualty animal’. Given the level of terror inflicted on these animals by these hunt thugs is it any wonder there are so many ‘casualty …

content:
Appel pour une manif autonome contre les frontières


10 octobre à 14h à Barbès


RDV

 à l'angle du boulevard de la chapelle et de la rue caplat


Depuis plusieurs années, le gouvernement est dans une marche en avant de plus en plus répressive, enferme toujours plus pour contenir la contestation sociale. Création de 3000 nouvelles places de taule, de super-prisons contre les narco trafiquants, de 11

CRA

 supplémentaires (les prisons pour les personnes n'ayant pas les bons papiers), entrée en vigueur du pacte asile immigration et du réglement retour pour rafler et expulser toujours plus facilement.


Tout ça dans un contexte global raciste et sécuritaire toujours plus étouffant, que ce soit à travers l'omniprésence des discours d'extrême droite dans l'espace public et médiatique, les meurtres policiers, les rafles, la surveillance généralisée et les politiques antisociales.


À l'échelle mondiale, la vie des gens est rythmée par les guerres, les génocides, les déportations, l'écocide...


Ces poussées et mouvements autoritaires et réactionnaires ne sont pas nouveaux et ne feront jamais taire la révolte des opprimé.es.s. Partout dans le monde, des gens se soulèvent et s'organisent. De La Paz à Tirana, en passant par les rues de Minneapolis contre

ICE

, les révoltés s'auto organisent pour lutter contre leurs oppresseurs.


En France aussi, les gens ne se résignent pas, que ce soit de façon spontanée face aux flics, en s'organisant collectivement face à un meurtre policier, dans des ag pour lutter contre les

CRA

 et les prisons, en attaquant et sabotant les infrastructures de ce monde de merde, ou encore en allant piller des magasins contre la vie chère. Cette liste est non exhaustive...


On voudrait nous faire croire que les seules perspectives politiques sont tournées vers les élections de 2027 et un avenir électoraliste, mais pour nous ça ne sera jamais une option.


Tant que les États existeront nous ne serons jamais libres et leurs frontières entraîneront leurs lots de morts, d'enfermé.es.s et de vies brisées. Et cela quelque soit la couleur politique du garde-frontières ou du trieur de bons ou mauvais migrants.


N'en déplaise aux promoteurs de la France insoummise, les politiques racistes n'ont jamais attendu l'extrême droite pour être mises en place.


Détruisons les États, les frontières, les partis et tout ce qui nous opprime.


On a besoin de reprendre la rue sans attendre qu'on nous l'autorise pour se rencontrer, faire de l'agitation, crier nos rages et notre envie de détruire leur monde pourrave

 

!


Rdv le Samedi 10 octobre à 14 h à Barbès à l'angle du boulevard de la Chapelle et de la rue Caplat


Des anarchistes contre les frontières

author: Habib Badawi
title: Beyond the Fighter Jets: What Algeria’s Deployment to Niger Really Signals
content:
Four Algerian

Su-30 fighters

 touched down in Niamey on 30 August 2026, trailed by an aerial refueling aircraft. A day earlier, mutinous soldiers — some drawn from units worn down by heavy losses fighting jihadist groups — had

stormed a military base next to the capital’s airport and moved on the presidential palace

. Niger’s government asked for help, and Algiers answered. Algeria’s Ministry of National Defense

described the deployment

 as a mission to support the Nigerien army and deepen strategic cooperation between the two countries. What has been less noticed was that these jets followed months of Algerian energy investment in Niger — a sequence explored below, and one that says more about Algiers’s intentions than the aircraft do.


While four jets are insufficient to alter the military balance in the Sahel, the political message conveyed by their deployment may be of greater significance than their quantity.


The central issue is not whether Algeria has become an expeditionary military power — by any conventional measure of force projection, it has not, at least not yet. Rather, the focus is on whether Algiers is redefining the boundaries of its perceived security interests. The events in Niger indicate that instability south of Algeria’s border is increasingly regarded as an extension of Algeria’s own strategic space, rather than as an external concern.


Beyond the fighter jets


Algeria’s current engagement in Niger in fact began several months ago. On 3 June, Algeria and Niger switched on a

40-megawatt power plant

 at Gorou Banda, on the edge of Niamey, which Algeria says its engineers built in under three months. A day earlier, subsidiaries of the state energy giant Sonatrach

signed three agreements

 with Niger’s national oil company, SONIDEP, covering seismic surveys, drilling, fuel distribution and training. And on 4 June, Algeria

broke ground

 on its stretch of the

Trans-Saharan Gas Pipeline

, a project designed to eventually link Nigeria’s gas fields to Europe through Niger and Algeria. All of this predates the mutiny by nearly three months. By the time the Su-30s landed, Algiers had already built Niger a power plant, signed three energy agreements, and broken ground on a pipeline — the deployment reads less as the start of a relationship than as Algiers protecting an

investment already made

.


Electricity, oil, gas and infrastructure increasingly bind the two countries — and lasting partnerships are usually built this way before arms ever enter the picture.


Algerian fighter jets have been deployed to Niger. Image source: afrinz.ru.


From caution to strategic depth


For decades, Algeria’s foreign policy has been defined by a near-sacred principle of non-intervention, a legacy of its own long and bloody struggle for independence. Libya’s collapse after 2011 complicated that instinct rather than simply reinforcing it: watching NATO’s intervention produce years of chaos next door hardened Algiers’s wariness of foreign military adventures, even as the resulting spillover of terrorism, arms and instability across its southern and eastern frontiers made the border itself too dangerous to ignore.


That reputation for caution deserves scrutiny in its own right. Algiers has for decades

backed the Polisario Front

 in

Western Sahara

 politically and materially, hosting its leadership and refugee camps on Algerian soil — support it frames as decolonisation, not intervention, and has never extended to its own uniformed troops. The real distinction, then, is less ‘non-intervention versus intervention’ than ‘indirect backing versus overt deployment.’ Seen that way, Niger is not a reversal of tradition but the crossing of a narrower threshold: Algeria’s own military, not proxies, operating beyond its borders.


In 2020, Algeria rewrote its constitution to allow, for the first time, the deployment of troops abroad.

Article 91

 lets the president send units of the People’s National Army outside Algeria’s borders, provided two-thirds of both chambers of parliament agree. The clause did not turn Algeria into an interventionist power overnight. It simply created a legal door that could be opened if the leadership judged it necessary.


For years, this legal provision remained unused. The intervention in Niger marks the first instance of its activation. Rather than abandoning its traditional caution, Algeria appears to be redefining its geographic boundaries; the southern border is now …

author: Julius Gavroche
title: Nation of Terrorists
content:
Matthew Wolfe on the use of domestic terrorism charges against activists, from the Earth Liberation Front to Prairieland.


from Verso Books

Blog

 03/09/2026


Late on the night of July 4, 2025, a group of eleven protesters walked up to the outside 

of the Prairieland Detention Center

 in Alvarado, Texas and began setting off fireworks. Prairieland serves as a holding facility for immigrants recently detained by ICE. Conditions inside the facility were widely reported to be inhumane. One woman, arrested on a warrant for an open traffic ticket, told the 

Washington Post

 that, due to a lack of beds, she was forced to sleep on a thin mat over a concrete floor. 

Another recalled

 being denied medical care and that the facility’s filthy tap water had “things swimming in it.” The fireworks, as the participants later testified, were part of a “noise demonstration,” a spectacle intended to show solidarity with detainees and bring attention to the Trump administration’s architecture of mass deportation. Hearing the booms, a confused jail staffer called 911, and local law enforcement was dispatched to the scene. Shortly after they arrived, a police lieutenant, spotting a man in a neon green gaiter holding a rifle, leveled his handgun and ordered the suspect to the ground. The man, a former Marine reservist, fired several shots in the direction of the officer, hitting him in the left shoulder above the clavicle.


In the aftermath, the protesters, including the former reservist, were arrested. Notably, so too were eleven other defendants who did not attend the protest at Prairieland but were accused of assisting the demonstrators in various ways. Among those in the latter category was Daniel Sanchez-Estrada, husband to one of the on-site protesters, who was indicted for moving a box of his wife’s anarchist literature – an effort, prosecutors claimed, to hide incriminating evidence. Another defendant was arrested for deleting a friend from a group chat. Federal officials would later describe the fireworks as “explosives” and contend the demonstration was actually a planned ambush designed to lure law enforcement officers to their deaths. As punishment, the defendants were sentenced to a combined 556 years in prison. For transporting his spouse’s zines, Sanchez-Estrada, convicted of “conspiracy to corruptly conceal documents,” received 30 years. Fifteen of the Prairieland defendants were also, in addition to other charges, indicted for providing “material support” to terrorists.


The Prairieland case was a signal moment in the Trump administration’s war on dissent, marking the first time it chose to bring terror charges against domestic political opponents. It will not be the last. Last September, several months after the shooting, Trump issued an executive order declaring “antifa” a domestic terrorist organization.

[1]

 A few days later, he issued a directive – the 

National Security Presidential Memorandum

, or NSPM-7 – instructing federal law enforcement agencies, including Joint Terrorism Task Forces, to counter a recent rise in “domestic terrorism” and “organized political violence.” An overtly partisan document, the NSPM-7 makes no mention of right-wing violence but cites the assassination of Charlie Kirk and attacks on ICE officers as grounds for new investigations into “anti-fascist” groups. Such groups, it notes, can be identified by their espousal of “anti-Americanism, anti-capitalism, and anti-Christianity … extremism on migration, race, and gender” and “hostility towards those who hold traditional American views on family, religion, and morality.” While in recent years prosecutors have shown an increasing willingness 

to pursue domestic terrorism charges against protesters

, the NSPM-7 represents a frightening shift in federal policy, one in which the formidable apparatus of the national security state is now aimed directly at the left. 


As observers of the Prairieland case have pointed out, “antifa,” “material support,” and “terrorism” have,  in the hands of the state, become distressingly limber phrases. “Antifa” now functions as a catch-all term for any left-ish demonstrator – that is, anyone who is plausibly anti-fascist. 

Faiza Patel of New York University’s Brennan Center,

 meanwhile, notes that “material support” for terrorism could be interpreted as broadly as buying a protester a meal or donating money.

[2]
